<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The share of a project&#x27;s output that would flow on a given line, used to split the cost of upgrading that line.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a06-interconnection.html">A6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="district-heating" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-district-heating">
<h3 id="glossary-name-district-heating"><a href="#district-heating">District heating</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Heat made in one place and piped as hot water or steam to warm many buildings.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="dominated-plan" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-dominated-plan">
<h3 id="glossary-name-dominated-plan"><a href="#dominated-plan">Dominated plan</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A plan that another plan beats on every count: no more cost, no more emissions, and better on at least one.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="12-trade-offs.html">lesson 12</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="dot-product" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-dot-product">
<h3 id="glossary-name-dot-product"><a href="#dot-product">Dot product</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The sum of the products of two vectors&#x27; matching entries, such as costs times outputs, added up.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k06-vectors-matrices.html">K6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="duck-curve" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-duck-curve">
<h3 id="glossary-name-duck-curve"><a href="#duck-curve">Duck curve</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The daily shape of demand minus solar output, with a dip at midday and a steep climb in the evening.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="02-demand.html">lesson 2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="dummy-variable" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-dummy-variable">
<h3 id="glossary-name-dummy-variable"><a href="#dummy-variable">Dummy variable</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A 0/1 flag in a regression, such as 1 for a home on the tariff and 0 for one that is not; its coefficient is the fitted difference between the two groups.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m14-did-it-work.html">M14</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="duration-curve" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-duration-curve">
<h3 id="glossary-name-duration-curve"><a href="#duration-curve">Duration curve</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A year of hourly values sorted from highest to lowest, showing for how many hours each level is reached.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="b02-python-data.html">B2</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-e" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-e">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-e">E</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="econometrics" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-econometrics">
<h3 id="glossary-name-econometrics"><a href="#econometrics">Econometrics</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Statistics applied to economic data, often to estimate whether a change caused an effect.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r10-question-studio.html">R10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="efficiency" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-efficiency">
<h3 id="glossary-name-efficiency"><a href="#efficiency">Efficiency</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The share of the energy put into a plant or device that comes out in the useful form, such as electricity.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k02-rates-efficiencies.html">K2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="eia" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-eia">
<h3 id="glossary-name-eia"><a href="#eia">EIA</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The Energy Information Administration, the statistics agency of the United States Department of Energy, which publishes data on energy production, use and prices.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf3-hydrogen-under-uncertainty.html">CF3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="elective-pay" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-elective-pay">
<h3 id="glossary-name-elective-pay"><a href="#elective-pay">Elective pay</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A rule of United States tax law that lets tax-exempt and governmental bodies, such as school districts, receive the value of certain clean-energy tax credits as a payment from the IRS.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="ck-a-spreadsheet.html">CK-A</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="electric-current" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-electric-current">
<h3 id="glossary-name-electric-current"><a href="#electric-current">Electric current</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The flow of electric charge through a wire, measured in amperes (A); for the same power, a higher voltage needs less current.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="electric-vehicle" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-electric-vehicle">
<h3 id="glossary-name-electric-vehicle"><a href="#electric-vehicle">Electric vehicle (EV)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A car, bus or truck driven by an electric motor from a battery charged from the grid, instead of by burning gasoline or diesel.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="sb3-city-planner.html">SB3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="electrification" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-electrification">
<h3 id="glossary-name-electrification"><a href="#electrification">Electrification</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Switching a use of energy, such as heating or driving, from burning fuel to using electricity.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="02-demand.html">lesson 2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="electrolyzer" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-electrolyzer">
<h3 id="glossary-name-electrolyzer"><a href="#electrolyzer">Electrolyzer</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A machine that uses electricity to split water into hydrogen and oxygen.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.html">CF2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="electrolyzer-stack" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-electrolyzer-stack">
<h3 id="glossary-name-electrolyzer-stack"><a href="#electrolyzer-stack">Electrolyzer stack</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The stack of cells inside an electrolyzer where electricity splits water into hydrogen and oxygen; it wears with use and is replaced several times over a plant&#x27;s life.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m11-tea-in-models.html">M11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="emission-factor" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-emission-factor">
<h3 id="glossary-name-emission-factor"><a href="#emission-factor">Emission factor</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The average mass of a pollutant released per unit of fuel burned or of output, such as kilograms of SO₂ per tonne of coal, taken from measurements.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f11-air-climate-people.html">F11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="emissions-cap" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-emissions-cap">
<h3 id="glossary-name-emissions-cap"><a href="#emissions-cap">Emissions cap</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A limit on the total CO2 that may be emitted in a period, such as a year.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="12-trade-offs.html">lesson 12</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="emissions-inventory" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-emissions-inventory">
<h3 id="glossary-name-emissions-inventory"><a href="#emissions-inventory">Emissions inventory</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An account that divides emissions that already happened among their sources or users, so that the shares add up to the total.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a10-emissions-questions.html">A10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="employment-multiplier" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-employment-multiplier">
<h3 id="glossary-name-employment-multiplier"><a href="#employment-multiplier">Employment multiplier</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The total jobs, on site plus at suppliers and from workers&#x27; spending, that go with each on-site job, taken from a regional input-output table.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a13-fairness-jobs.html">A13</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="energization" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-energization">
<h3 id="glossary-name-energization"><a href="#energization">Energization</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Switching on a customer&#x27;s grid service, so that power can flow to it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf7-cost-of-waiting.html">CF7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="energy" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-energy">
<h3 id="glossary-name-energy"><a href="#energy">Energy</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An amount of electricity made or used over a stretch of time, equal to power multiplied by time and measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh) or megawatt-hours (MWh).</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="00-grid-operator.html">lesson 0</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="energy-attribute-certificate" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-energy-attribute-certificate">
<h3 id="glossary-name-energy-attribute-certificate"><a href="#energy-attribute-certificate">Energy attribute certificate (EAC)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A tradable record that one megawatt-hour was generated by a given plant at a given place and time, which a buyer retires to claim that power; a rule decides which certificates may count.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m11-tea-in-models.html">M11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="energy-burden" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-energy-burden">
<h3 id="glossary-name-energy-burden"><a href="#energy-burden">Energy burden</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The share of a household&#x27;s income spent on energy bills.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a22-tradeoff-explorer.html">A22</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="energy-carrier" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-energy-carrier">
<h3 id="glossary-name-energy-carrier"><a href="#energy-carrier">Energy carrier</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A form in which energy is moved to where it is used, such as electricity, natural gas, gasoline or hydrogen.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f03-energy-services.html">F3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="energy-hub" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-energy-hub">
<h3 id="glossary-name-energy-hub"><a href="#energy-hub">Energy hub</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A model of energy carriers coming in, being converted and stored, and meeting the uses inside a chosen boundary: a building, a campus, a district or a city.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="sb3-city-planner.html">SB3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="energy-security" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-energy-security">
<h3 id="glossary-name-energy-security"><a href="#energy-security">Energy security</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Keeping energy flowing at bearable prices when a fuel, a supplier or a route is cut off.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a22-tradeoff-explorer.html">A22</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="energy-service" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-energy-service">
<h3 id="glossary-name-energy-service"><a href="#energy-service">Energy service</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">What people actually want from energy, such as a warm room, hot water, cold food, light or a trip; the energy is only the means.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f03-energy-services.html">F3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="energy-storage" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-energy-storage">
<h3 id="glossary-name-energy-storage"><a href="#energy-storage">Energy storage</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Equipment, such as a battery, that takes in electricity at one time and gives it back later, with some losses.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="09-storage.html">lesson 9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="energy-only-market" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-energy-only-market">
<h3 id="glossary-name-energy-only-market"><a href="#energy-only-market">Energy-only market</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A wholesale market design with no separate capacity market, in which energy and reserve prices, high in scarce hours, must pay for capacity that is rarely used.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a03-market-design.html">A3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="enrichment" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-enrichment">
<h3 id="glossary-name-enrichment"><a href="#enrichment">Enrichment (of uranium)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Raising the share of uranium-235 in uranium: natural uranium has just over 0.7%, and power-plant fuel in the United States 3% to 5%.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="epsg-code" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-epsg-code">
<h3 id="glossary-name-epsg-code"><a href="#epsg-code">EPSG code</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A catalog number that names one coordinate system exactly, such as EPSG:4326 for latitude and longitude in degrees.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r04-data.html">R4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="epsilon-constraint" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-epsilon-constraint">
<h3 id="glossary-name-epsilon-constraint"><a href="#epsilon-constraint">Epsilon-constraint method</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A way to trace a trade-off by optimizing one goal while capping the other, then moving the cap step by step.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="12-trade-offs.html">lesson 12</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="equal-area-projection" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-equal-area-projection">
<h3 id="glossary-name-equal-area-projection"><a href="#equal-area-projection">Equal-area projection</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A map projection that keeps areas true, at the cost of shapes and distances; Albers equal-area (EPSG:5070) is the usual one for the contiguous U.S.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r04-data.html">R4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="equivalent-firm-capacity" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-equivalent-firm-capacity">
<h3 id="glossary-name-equivalent-firm-capacity"><a href="#equivalent-firm-capacity">Equivalent firm capacity</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The MW of a perfect, always-available plant that would make a grid as reliable as a given resource does; divided by the resource&#x27;s MW, it is an accreditation.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a05-adequacy.html">A5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="ercot" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-ercot">
<h3 id="glossary-name-ercot"><a href="#ercot">ERCOT</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The Electric Reliability Council of Texas: the grid operator, and its wholesale market, for most of Texas.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.html">CF2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="ethics-board" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-ethics-board">
<h3 id="glossary-name-ethics-board"><a href="#ethics-board">Ethics board (IRB)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The committee that reviews research with people before it starts; in the United States, an institutional review board.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r09-integrity-stakeholders.html">R9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="ethnography" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-ethnography">
<h3 id="glossary-name-ethnography"><a href="#ethnography">Ethnography</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A research method of long observation and conversation with people where they live or work, to understand their routines in their own terms.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="x06-social-methods.html">X6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="event-study" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-event-study">
<h3 id="glossary-name-event-study"><a href="#event-study">Event study</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A difference-in-differences estimated period by period around the start date, so the periods before the start can be checked for parallel trends.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m14-did-it-work.html">M14</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="evidence-ladder" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-evidence-ladder">
<h3 id="glossary-name-evidence-ladder"><a href="#evidence-ladder">Evidence ladder</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The stages a project climbs: announced, funded, permitted, under construction, operating and at design output.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="n01-news-lens.html">N1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="evidentiary-hearing" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-evidentiary-hearing">
<h3 id="glossary-name-evidentiary-hearing"><a href="#evidentiary-hearing">Evidentiary hearing</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A formal hearing at which the parties present their evidence and question each other&#x27;s witnesses before the commissioners.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="x04-rules-law.html">X4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="ex-post-review" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-ex-post-review">
<h3 id="glossary-name-ex-post-review"><a href="#ex-post-review">Ex-post review</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An evaluation made after a program or project has run, comparing what happened with what was planned or expected.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r01-framing.html">R1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="exajoule" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-exajoule">
<h3 id="glossary-name-exajoule"><a href="#exajoule">Exajoule (EJ)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A unit of energy equal to a thousand petajoules (10^18 joules, about 278 TWh), used for the yearly energy of a whole country.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="exclusion-layer" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-exclusion-layer">
<h3 id="glossary-name-exclusion-layer"><a href="#exclusion-layer">Exclusion layer</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A map layer that removes land from a siting screen outright, whatever else the land offers, because a rule or a hard limit forbids building there.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a19-gis-siting.html">A19</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="exogenous" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-exogenous">
<h3 id="glossary-name-exogenous"><a href="#exogenous">Exogenous</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Set from outside a model as an input, rather than worked out by the model.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf7-cost-of-waiting.html">CF7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="expected-unserved-energy" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-expected-unserved-energy">
<h3 id="glossary-name-expected-unserved-energy"><a href="#expected-unserved-energy">Expected unserved energy</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Demand left unmet, averaged over many simulated years, in MWh a year: an amount of energy, unlike a load&#x27;s size in MW.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r03-system-and-method.html">R3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="expected-value" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-expected-value">
<h3 id="glossary-name-expected-value"><a href="#expected-value">Expected value</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The long-run average of an uncertain quantity: each possible outcome multiplied by its chance, then added up.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k05-probability-statistics.html">K5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="evpi" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-evpi">
<h3 id="glossary-name-evpi"><a href="#evpi">Expected value of perfect information (EVPI)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How much a perfect forecast would save, in expectation, against the stochastic plan: the most such a forecast is worth to a planner who weighs only expected cost.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m08-stochastic-robust.html">M8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="expected-value-problem" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-expected-value-problem">
<h3 id="glossary-name-expected-value-problem"><a href="#expected-value-problem">Expected-value problem</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The planning problem solved for one average future, every uncertain input set to its mean; its plan is then priced in the real branches.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m08-stochastic-robust.html">M8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="exploratory-scenario" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-exploratory-scenario">
<h3 id="glossary-name-exploratory-scenario"><a href="#exploratory-scenario">Exploratory scenario</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A scenario that fixes its assumptions about demand, prices, policies and costs and asks what follows, without forcing any result; the IEA&#x27;s Current Policies and Stated Policies scenarios are of this kind.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a20-national-scenarios.html">A20</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="external-cost" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-external-cost">
<h3 id="glossary-name-external-cost"><a href="#external-cost">External cost</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A cost that falls on people outside a deal, such as the damage from CO₂, which neither the buyer nor the seller pays.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf7-cost-of-waiting.html">CF7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="extreme-period" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-extreme-period">
<h3 id="glossary-name-extreme-period"><a href="#extreme-period">Extreme period</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An unusually demanding stretch of time, such as a cold, still week with high demand and little wind, kept in a model so its plan copes with it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r02-literature.html">R2</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-f" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-f">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-f">F</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="falsification-statement" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-falsification-statement">
<h3 id="glossary-name-falsification-statement"><a href="#falsification-statement">Falsification statement</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A sentence naming the result that would show your expected answer wrong.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r01-framing.html">R1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="fast-frequency-response" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-fast-frequency-response">
<h3 id="glossary-name-fast-frequency-response"><a href="#fast-frequency-response">Fast frequency response</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Power from batteries or other inverter-based resources delivered within a fraction of a second of a frequency drop.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="03-balancing.html">lesson 3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="fault" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-fault">
<h3 id="glossary-name-fault"><a href="#fault">Fault</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An unintended electrical path, such as a fallen branch joining a wire to the ground, through which a large current rushes until a protective device opens.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="feasible-region" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-feasible-region">
<h3 id="glossary-name-feasible-region"><a href="#feasible-region">Feasible region</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The set of all plans that meet every rule of a model; on a two-variable chart it is a shaded polygon.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="10-write-it-down.html">lesson 10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="feature" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-feature">
<h3 id="glossary-name-feature"><a href="#feature">Feature</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">One input a model learns from, such as the same hour yesterday or the day of the week.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m10-ml-forecasting.html">M10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="feedback-loop" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-feedback-loop">
<h3 id="glossary-name-feedback-loop"><a href="#feedback-loop">Feedback loop</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A chain of causes that leads back to where it started, so a change comes back to push on itself.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f02-systems-and-map.html">F2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="feeder" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-feeder">
<h3 id="glossary-name-feeder"><a href="#feeder">Feeder</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A distribution line that carries power from a substation to the homes and businesses along it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f01-five-scales.html">F1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="feedstock" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-feedstock">
<h3 id="glossary-name-feedstock"><a href="#feedstock">Feedstock</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A material a process consumes to make its product, as an ammonia plant consumes hydrogen.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a16-hydrogen-ptx.html">A16</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="ferc" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-ferc">
<h3 id="glossary-name-ferc"><a href="#ferc">FERC (Federal Energy Regulatory Commission)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The federal regulator of interstate electricity transmission, wholesale power sales and interstate gas pipelines in the United States.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f09-city-energy.html">F9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="fermi-estimate" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-fermi-estimate">
<h3 id="glossary-name-fermi-estimate"><a href="#fermi-estimate">Fermi estimate</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A quick estimate built from round numbers and a few simple steps, aiming to get the order of magnitude right.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="01-power-energy.html">lesson 1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="final-energy" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-final-energy">
<h3 id="glossary-name-final-energy"><a href="#final-energy">Final energy</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The energy a home, business or vehicle buys and uses, as on its meters and receipts, such as kWh of electricity or gallons of gasoline.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f03-energy-services.html">F3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="financial-security" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-financial-security">
<h3 id="glossary-name-financial-security"><a href="#financial-security">Financial security</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Money, or a guarantee such as a letter of credit, that a customer pledges so that the utility or grid operator is covered if the customer backs out or does not pay.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a06-interconnection.html">A6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="fine-particles" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-fine-particles">
<h3 id="glossary-name-fine-particles"><a href="#fine-particles">Fine particles (PM2.5)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Airborne particles no wider than 2.5 micrometers, small enough to reach deep into the lungs; burning releases them and also forms them in the air from SO₂ and NOx.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f11-air-climate-people.html">F11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="firm-capacity" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-firm-capacity">
<h3 id="glossary-name-firm-capacity"><a href="#firm-capacity">Firm capacity</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Capacity a grid counts on in its riskiest hours, such as a still, dark evening: a planning rating of what a plant adds to reliability, not output promised in every hour.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="06-three-jobs.html">lesson 6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="firm-load-shed" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-firm-load-shed">
<h3 id="glossary-name-firm-load-shed"><a href="#firm-load-shed">Firm load shed</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Disconnecting customers whose supply is normally assured, on the grid operator&#x27;s order and usually in rotation, so that a grid short of supply does not collapse.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a09-hazards.html">A9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="firm-output" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-firm-output">
<h3 id="glossary-name-firm-output"><a href="#firm-output">Firm output</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Power a plant can be counted on to deliver steadily, such as the same output in every hour; also called stabilized output.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.html">CF2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="firm-share" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-firm-share">
<h3 id="glossary-name-firm-share"><a href="#firm-share">Firm share (ELCC)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The share of a plant&#x27;s capacity that a grid credits toward its reliability needs, often estimated as its effective load-carrying capability (ELCC) and set per technology class; a planning rating, not output guaranteed in any hour.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="06-three-jobs.html">lesson 6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="fission" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-fission">
<h3 id="glossary-name-fission"><a href="#fission">Fission</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The splitting of a heavy atom, such as uranium-235, into two smaller atoms when it absorbs a neutron, which releases heat and a few new neutrons.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="fixed-charge" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-fixed-charge">
<h3 id="glossary-name-fixed-charge"><a href="#fixed-charge">Fixed charge</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A part of a power bill that is the same each month however much electricity the home uses.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a22-tradeoff-explorer.html">A22</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="fixed-om" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-fixed-om">
<h3 id="glossary-name-fixed-om"><a href="#fixed-om">Fixed O&amp;M</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Operation and maintenance costs a plant pays every year whether or not it runs, such as staff and insurance.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="07-cost.html">lesson 7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="flexibility" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-flexibility">
<h3 id="glossary-name-flexibility"><a href="#flexibility">Flexibility</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The ability of a plant, a store or a group of users to raise or lower power quickly when the grid asks.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="06-three-jobs.html">lesson 6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="flood-zone" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-flood-zone">
<h3 id="glossary-name-flood-zone"><a href="#flood-zone">Flood zone</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Land mapped as likely to flood; in the U.S., FEMA&#x27;s Special Flood Hazard Area is land with at least a 1% chance of flooding in any year.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a19-gis-siting.html">A19</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="flow" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-flow">
<h3 id="glossary-name-flow"><a href="#flow">Flow</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A rate that fills or drains a stock, such as megawatts into a battery or tonnes of CO₂ a year; only flows change a stock.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f02-systems-and-map.html">F2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="flow-based-coupling" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-flow-based-coupling">
<h3 id="glossary-name-flow-based-coupling"><a href="#flow-based-coupling">Flow-based market coupling</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A form of market coupling that limits trades by how much power would flow on each critical line of the grid, rather than by a fixed amount per border.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="forced-outage-rate" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-forced-outage-rate">
<h3 id="glossary-name-forced-outage-rate"><a href="#forced-outage-rate">Forced outage rate</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The share of time a power plant is unexpectedly out of service, waiting for repair, rather than out for planned maintenance.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a05-adequacy.html">A5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="forecast-error" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-forecast-error">
<h3 id="glossary-name-forecast-error"><a href="#forecast-error">Forecast error</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The difference between what was forecast, such as tomorrow&#x27;s demand or wind, and what actually happened.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="04-forecasts.html">lesson 4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="forecast-horizon" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-forecast-horizon">
<h3 id="glossary-name-forecast-horizon"><a href="#forecast-horizon">Forecast horizon</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How far ahead of the moment it is made a forecast looks, such as one hour or one day.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m10-ml-forecasting.html">M10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="frozen-telemetry" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-frozen-telemetry">
<h3 id="glossary-name-frozen-telemetry"><a href="#frozen-telemetry">Frozen telemetry</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A measurement feed stuck on its last value, which shows up as the same reading hour after hour.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="b02-python-data.html">B2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="fuel-assembly" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-fuel-assembly">
<h3 id="glossary-name-fuel-assembly"><a href="#fuel-assembly">Fuel assembly</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A bundle of fuel rods, each a sealed metal tube of stacked uranium pellets, loaded into a reactor core as one unit.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="fuel-cell" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-fuel-cell">
<h3 id="glossary-name-fuel-cell"><a href="#fuel-cell">Fuel cell</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A device that turns hydrogen (and oxygen from the air) into electricity, with water as the by-product: an electrolyzer run backwards.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.html">CF2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="full-cycle" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-full-cycle">
<h3 id="glossary-name-full-cycle"><a href="#full-cycle">Full cycle</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Charging a store&#x27;s usable energy once and discharging it once; two half charges and discharges count as one full cycle.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a08-storage-duration.html">A8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="full-load-hours" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-full-load-hours">
<h3 id="glossary-name-full-load-hours"><a href="#full-load-hours">Full-load hours</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Output over a period divided by rated capacity, giving the equivalent hours at full output; dividing by the hours in that period gives average utilization.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a16-hydrogen-ptx.html">A16</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="functional-unit" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-functional-unit">
<h3 id="glossary-name-functional-unit"><a href="#functional-unit">Functional unit</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The amount of service a footprint is counted per, such as one kWh made or one MWh used, so that options are compared on the same service.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a11-lca-nexus.html">A11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="fuse" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-fuse">
<h3 id="glossary-name-fuse"><a href="#fuse">Fuse</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A wire that melts on a fault and cuts the power beyond it; a crew must replace it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-g" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-g">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-g">G</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="gas-reformer" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-gas-reformer">
<h3 id="glossary-name-gas-reformer"><a href="#gas-reformer">Gas reformer</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A plant that makes hydrogen from natural gas and steam, releasing carbon dioxide unless it is captured.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m08-stochastic-robust.html">M8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="gas-turbine" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-gas-turbine">
<h3 id="glossary-name-gas-turbine"><a href="#gas-turbine">Gas turbine</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An engine that compresses air, burns fuel in it and lets the hot gas spin a turbine, as a jet engine does; alone it is a simple-cycle plant, such as a peaker.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="gaussian-process" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-gaussian-process">
<h3 id="glossary-name-gaussian-process"><a href="#gaussian-process">Gaussian process</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A way to fit a smooth curve to a few points that also draws a band around it: narrow near the points, wider where there are none.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m09-surrogates-uq.html">M9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="gdp-deflator" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-gdp-deflator">
<h3 id="glossary-name-gdp-deflator"><a href="#gdp-deflator">GDP deflator</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A price index for everything an economy produces; multiplying by the ratio of two years&#x27; values turns one year&#x27;s dollars into another&#x27;s, such as 2022 dollars into 2025 dollars.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a18-city-plan.html">A18</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="generator" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-generator">
<h3 id="glossary-name-generator"><a href="#generator">Generator</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A machine that turns the spin of a shaft into electricity, by turning magnets past coils of wire.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="geothermal" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-geothermal">
<h3 id="glossary-name-geothermal"><a href="#geothermal">Geothermal power</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Electricity made from the earth&#x27;s heat, using hot water or steam brought up from wells.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="gigawatt" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-gigawatt">
<h3 id="glossary-name-gigawatt"><a href="#gigawatt">Gigawatt (GW)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A thousand megawatts, a rate of energy flow used for large plants, whole fleets and national demand.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="n01-news-lens.html">N1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="gigawatt-hour" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-gigawatt-hour">
<h3 id="glossary-name-gigawatt-hour"><a href="#gigawatt-hour">Gigawatt-hour (GWh)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A unit of energy equal to a million kilowatt-hours, used for the yearly energy of a city, a large plant or a large customer.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f09-city-energy.html">F9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="gis" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-gis">
<h3 id="glossary-name-gis"><a href="#gis">GIS (geographic information system)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Software and methods for mapping and analyzing data tied to places, such as land use, lines and population.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r10-question-studio.html">R10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="global-sensitivity-analysis" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-global-sensitivity-analysis">
<h3 id="glossary-name-global-sensitivity-analysis"><a href="#global-sensitivity-analysis">Global sensitivity analysis</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Ranking a model&#x27;s inputs by their influence on a result while all of them vary together across their assumed ranges, rather than one at a time.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m07-monte-carlo.html">M7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="global-warming-potential" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-global-warming-potential">
<h3 id="glossary-name-global-warming-potential"><a href="#global-warming-potential">Global warming potential (GWP)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How much a tonne of a gas warms the climate over a chosen horizon, such as 100 years, compared with a tonne of CO₂.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f11-air-climate-people.html">F11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="governor" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-governor">
<h3 id="glossary-name-governor"><a href="#governor">Governor</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A plant&#x27;s speed control that opens or closes its steam, gas or water valves as the grid frequency changes.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="03-balancing.html">lesson 3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="gpc" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-gpc">
<h3 id="glossary-name-gpc"><a href="#gpc">GPC</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The Global Protocol for Community-Scale Greenhouse Gas Emission Inventories (WRI, C40 Cities and ICLEI, 2014), the common standard for counting a city&#x27;s emissions by sector and scope.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a18-city-plan.html">A18</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="green-hydrogen" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-green-hydrogen">
<h3 id="glossary-name-green-hydrogen"><a href="#green-hydrogen">Green hydrogen</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Hydrogen made by electrolysis with renewable electricity, such as wind or solar power, rather than from natural gas.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf3-hydrogen-under-uncertainty.html">CF3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="frequency" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-frequency">
<h3 id="glossary-name-frequency"><a href="#frequency">Grid frequency</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The number of cycles per second of the grid&#x27;s alternating current, 60 hertz (Hz) in North America, which falls when power is short and rises when there is too much.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="00-grid-operator.html">lesson 0</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="grid-following" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-grid-following">
<h3 id="glossary-name-grid-following"><a href="#grid-following">Grid-following</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Said of an inverter, such as an ordinary solar inverter, that follows a voltage something else sets and stops when there is none.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f07-microgrids.html">F7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="grid-forming" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-grid-forming">
<h3 id="glossary-name-grid-forming"><a href="#grid-forming">Grid-forming</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Said of an inverter or a generator that sets voltage and frequency itself, so it can hold an island with no grid behind it; starting a dead island also takes equipment designed for that.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f07-microgrids.html">F7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="gross-calorific-value" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-gross-calorific-value">
<h3 id="glossary-name-gross-calorific-value"><a href="#gross-calorific-value">Gross calorific value</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The heat a fuel gives when burned, counting the heat won back by condensing the water vapor it forms; it is a little higher than the net value, which the IEA and Eurostat use.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="gdp" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-gdp">
<h3 id="glossary-name-gdp"><a href="#gdp">Gross domestic product (GDP)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The value of all the goods and services an economy produces in a year.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a21-security-minerals.html">A21</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="gross-jobs" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-gross-jobs">
<h3 id="glossary-name-gross-jobs"><a href="#gross-jobs">Gross jobs</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The jobs a project creates, counted on their own, without subtracting jobs lost or work that would have happened anyway.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a13-fairness-jobs.html">A13</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-h" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-h">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-h">H</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="git-head" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-git-head">
<h3 id="glossary-name-git-head"><a href="#git-head">HEAD (Git)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Git&#x27;s name for the commit you are on now; usually it points at a branch label, which points at that commit.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="hydraulic-head" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-hydraulic-head">
<h3 id="glossary-name-hydraulic-head"><a href="#hydraulic-head">Head (hydropower)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The height the water falls through a hydro plant, from the reservoir&#x27;s surface down to where it leaves the turbine, in meters.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="headroom" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-headroom">
<h3 id="glossary-name-headroom"><a href="#headroom">Headroom</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The spare capacity a line or other piece of equipment has left before it reaches its limit.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a06-interconnection.html">A6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="reserve-headroom" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-reserve-headroom">
<h3 id="glossary-name-reserve-headroom"><a href="#reserve-headroom">Headroom (for reserves)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The output a running unit could still add, or the load it could still shed, which it can offer to the grid as a reserve.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf4-existing-reactors-hydrogen.html">CF4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="heat-balance" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-heat-balance">
<h3 id="glossary-name-heat-balance"><a href="#heat-balance">Heat balance (steam-table)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An account of the energy entering and leaving each part of a steam cycle, using tables of steam&#x27;s properties at each pressure and temperature.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf5-drawing-the-boundary.html">CF5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="heat-engine" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-heat-engine">
<h3 id="glossary-name-heat-engine"><a href="#heat-engine">Heat engine</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A machine that turns part of a flow of heat into motion, such as a steam or gas turbine; the hotter its heat source, the larger the part it can turn.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="heat-exchanger" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-heat-exchanger">
<h3 id="glossary-name-heat-exchanger"><a href="#heat-exchanger">Heat exchanger</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A device that passes heat from one fluid to another through a wall, without mixing them; heat flows only from the hotter fluid to the cooler one.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="heat-pump" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-heat-pump">
<h3 id="glossary-name-heat-pump"><a href="#heat-pump">Heat pump</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A device that uses electricity to move heat, into a building to warm it or out of it to cool it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="02-demand.html">lesson 2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="heat-rate" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-heat-rate">
<h3 id="glossary-name-heat-rate"><a href="#heat-rate">Heat rate</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The fuel energy a power plant burns to make one megawatt-hour, for example in MMBtu per MWh, so lower means more efficient.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="07-cost.html">lesson 7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="hrsg" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-hrsg">
<h3 id="glossary-name-hrsg"><a href="#hrsg">Heat recovery steam generator (HRSG)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The boiler of a combined-cycle plant, heated by the gas turbine&#x27;s hot exhaust instead of a flame.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="heat-pump-water-heater" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-heat-pump-water-heater">
<h3 id="glossary-name-heat-pump-water-heater"><a href="#heat-pump-water-heater">Heat-pump water heater</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A water heater that moves heat from the surrounding air into the tank, using a fraction of the electricity an electric-resistance heater needs.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a15-efficiency-electrification.html">A15</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="heating-degree-days" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-heating-degree-days">
<h3 id="glossary-name-heating-degree-days"><a href="#heating-degree-days">Heating degree days</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A measure of how cold a year was: for each day, the degrees by which its average temperature fell below a base such as 18 °C, added over the year.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="held-out-data" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-held-out-data">
<h3 id="glossary-name-held-out-data"><a href="#held-out-data">Held-out data</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Records kept aside while a model is fitted and used only to score it, so the score shows how it does on data it has not seen.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m09-surrogates-uq.html">M9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="here-and-now" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-here-and-now">
<h3 id="glossary-name-here-and-now"><a href="#here-and-now">Here-and-now decision</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A decision that must be made before an uncertainty resolves, such as the size of a plant, and so is the same in every branch.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m08-stochastic-robust.html">M8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="hhi" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-hhi">
<h3 id="glossary-name-hhi"><a href="#hhi">Herfindahl-Hirschman index (HHI)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A measure of how concentrated a supply is: the sum of each supplier&#x27;s squared percentage share, from near 0 for many small suppliers to 10,000 for one.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a21-security-minerals.html">A21</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="hidden-state" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-hidden-state">
<h3 id="glossary-name-hidden-state"><a href="#hidden-state">Hidden state</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Values in a notebook&#x27;s memory that no longer match the code on the page, for example after a cell was edited but not rerun.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="high-temperature-electrolyzer" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-high-temperature-electrolyzer">
<h3 id="glossary-name-high-temperature-electrolyzer"><a href="#high-temperature-electrolyzer">High-temperature electrolyzer</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An electrolyzer that splits steam at several hundred degrees Celsius; part of the energy comes as heat, so it needs less electricity per kilogram.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.html">CF2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="histogram" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-histogram">
<h3 id="glossary-name-histogram"><a href="#histogram">Histogram</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A chart that sorts values into bins of equal width and shows how many fall in each bin.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k05-probability-statistics.html">K5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="horizon" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-horizon">
<h3 id="glossary-name-horizon"><a href="#horizon">Horizon</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The span of time a study covers, from a day of operation to decades of planning.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r03-system-and-method.html">R3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="hosting-capacity" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-hosting-capacity">
<h3 id="glossary-name-hosting-capacity"><a href="#hosting-capacity">Hosting capacity</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How much solar or other generation a feeder can take, at its existing settings and without upgrades, before a limit such as its voltage band is crossed.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a17-physical-feasibility.html">A17</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="hour-ending" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-hour-ending">
<h3 id="glossary-name-hour-ending"><a href="#hour-ending">Hour ending</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A time stamp that labels each hour by its last moment, so 01:00 means the hour from midnight to 01:00.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="b02-python-data.html">B2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="hourly-matching" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-hourly-matching">
<h3 id="glossary-name-hourly-matching"><a href="#hourly-matching">Hourly matching</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A rule that each hour&#x27;s electricity use is covered by clean generation in that same hour, rather than over a whole year.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a16-hydrogen-ptx.html">A16</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="hvdc" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-hvdc">
<h3 id="glossary-name-hvdc"><a href="#hvdc">HVDC (high-voltage direct current)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A transmission link that carries power as direct current, used for long undersea cables and to join grids that do not run in step.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-i" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-i">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-i">I</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="implied-carbon-price" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-implied-carbon-price">
<h3 id="glossary-name-implied-carbon-price"><a href="#implied-carbon-price">Implied carbon price</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A carbon price found, not set in advance, so that a plan just meets an emissions limit: on a page that tries prices, the lowest that meets it; in a least-cost linear program, the limit&#x27;s shadow price, the cost saved per tonne by a small relaxation.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a20-national-scenarios.html">A20</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="import-dependence" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-import-dependence">
<h3 id="glossary-name-import-dependence"><a href="#import-dependence">Import dependence</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A country&#x27;s net energy imports as a share of the energy it uses (its primary energy supply; Eurostat divides by gross available energy), negative for a net exporter; its value depends on how primary energy is counted.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="income-based-charge" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-income-based-charge">
<h3 id="glossary-name-income-based-charge"><a href="#income-based-charge">Income-based charge</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A utility charge that varies with household income, such as a fixed charge set in a few income tiers.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a13-fairness-jobs.html">A13</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="incremental-analysis" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-incremental-analysis">
<h3 id="glossary-name-incremental-analysis"><a href="#incremental-analysis">Incremental analysis</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Judging an addition by the difference between the system with it and the system without it, so that costs and earnings that exist either way drop out.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m11-tea-in-models.html">M11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="independent-events" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-independent-events">
<h3 id="glossary-name-independent-events"><a href="#independent-events">Independent events</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Events where knowing that one happened says nothing about whether the other did, so the chance of both is the product of their chances.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k05-probability-statistics.html">K5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="inequality" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-inequality">
<h3 id="glossary-name-inequality"><a href="#inequality">Inequality</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A rule that allows a range of values, written with ≤ (at most) or ≥ (at least).</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k04-linear-equations.html">K4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="inertia" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-inertia">
<h3 id="glossary-name-inertia"><a href="#inertia">Inertia</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Energy stored in the spinning machines of a power grid; it slows a fall in frequency but cannot stop it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="03-balancing.html">lesson 3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="infeasible" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-infeasible">
<h3 id="glossary-name-infeasible"><a href="#infeasible">Infeasible</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Said of a model whose rules contradict each other, so that no plan meets them all.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="10-write-it-down.html">lesson 10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="inflation" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-inflation">
<h3 id="glossary-name-inflation"><a href="#inflation">Inflation</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The rise in prices in general over time, so that a dollar buys less each year.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a01-project-tea.html">A1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="informed-consent" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-informed-consent">
<h3 id="glossary-name-informed-consent"><a href="#informed-consent">Informed consent</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A person&#x27;s agreement to take part in research, given freely after being told what will happen, the risks and how their data will be used.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r09-integrity-stakeholders.html">R9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="interconnection-agreement" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-interconnection-agreement">
<h3 id="glossary-name-interconnection-agreement"><a href="#interconnection-agreement">Interconnection agreement</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The contract that sets how and when a project connects, which upgrades are built and who pays for them.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a06-interconnection.html">A6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="interconnection-queue" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-interconnection-queue">
<h3 id="glossary-name-interconnection-queue"><a href="#interconnection-queue">Interconnection queue</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The list of projects asking to connect to the grid, each waiting for studies, upgrades and an agreement before it may run.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a06-interconnection.html">A6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="interconnection-request" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-interconnection-request">
<h3 id="glossary-name-interconnection-request"><a href="#interconnection-request">Interconnection request</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A project&#x27;s formal application to connect to the grid, filed with the transmission provider together with a deposit.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a06-interconnection.html">A6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="internal-rate-of-return" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-internal-rate-of-return">
<h3 id="glossary-name-internal-rate-of-return"><a href="#internal-rate-of-return">Internal rate of return (IRR)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The discount rate at which a project&#x27;s net present value is exactly zero: the return the project itself earns.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a01-project-tea.html">A1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="interquartile-range" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-interquartile-range">
<h3 id="glossary-name-interquartile-range"><a href="#interquartile-range">Interquartile range</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The middle half of a set of values, from the 25th to the 75th percentile.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a11-lca-nexus.html">A11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="intervenor" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-intervenor">
<h3 id="glossary-name-intervenor"><a href="#intervenor">Intervenor</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A person or organization that formally joins a regulatory case as a party, so it can file testimony and question witnesses.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="x04-rules-law.html">X4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="inverter" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-inverter">
<h3 id="glossary-name-inverter"><a href="#inverter">Inverter</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Power electronics that convert the direct current of solar panels and batteries, or a wind turbine&#x27;s varying output, into the grid&#x27;s alternating current.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="03-balancing.html">lesson 3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="investment-credit" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-investment-credit">
<h3 id="glossary-name-investment-credit"><a href="#investment-credit">Investment credit</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A payment, often through the tax code, of a share of what a new plant costs to build, whatever it later produces.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a12-policy-instruments.html">A12</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="investor-owned-utility" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-investor-owned-utility">
<h3 id="glossary-name-investor-owned-utility"><a href="#investor-owned-utility">Investor-owned utility</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An electric or gas utility owned by shareholders; its retail rates are typically set or approved by the state&#x27;s utility commission.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f09-city-energy.html">F9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="islanding" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-islanding">
<h3 id="glossary-name-islanding"><a href="#islanding">Islanding</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A microgrid or part of a grid disconnecting from the main grid and keeping its own loads supplied.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f01-five-scales.html">F1</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-j" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-j">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-j">J</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="job-year" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-job-year">
<h3 id="glossary-name-job-year"><a href="#job-year">Job-year</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">One person working full time for one year; 100 workers for six months make 50 job-years.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f08-large-loads.html">F8</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-k" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-k">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-k">K</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="kernel-density-estimate" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-kernel-density-estimate">
<h3 id="glossary-name-kernel-density-estimate"><a href="#kernel-density-estimate">Kernel density estimate</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A smooth estimate of where data points are dense, made by placing a small bump on every point and adding them up; sampling from it keeps the data&#x27;s shape with fewer points.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf8-power-curves-from-scarce-data.html">CF8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="kilowatt" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-kilowatt">
<h3 id="glossary-name-kilowatt"><a href="#kilowatt">Kilowatt (kW)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A unit of power equal to 1,000 watts.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="01-power-energy.html">lesson 1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="kilowatt-hour" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-kilowatt-hour">
<h3 id="glossary-name-kilowatt-hour"><a href="#kilowatt-hour">Kilowatt-hour (kWh)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The unit of energy on a household electricity bill: one kilowatt kept up for one hour.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="01-power-energy.html">lesson 1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="kw-dc" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-kw-dc">
<h3 id="glossary-name-kw-dc"><a href="#kw-dc">kW-DC</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A solar array&#x27;s size as the combined direct-current rated power of its panels at standard test conditions, while its actual output varies with sunlight, temperature and the inverter&#x27;s limits.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="ck-a-spreadsheet.html">CK-A</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-l" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-l">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-l">L</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="land-use-intensity" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-land-use-intensity">
<h3 id="glossary-name-land-use-intensity"><a href="#land-use-intensity">Land-use intensity</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The land a plant holds for each unit of energy it makes in a year, here square meters per MWh a year.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a11-lca-nexus.html">A11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="large-load" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-large-load">
<h3 id="glossary-name-large-load"><a href="#large-load">Large load</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">One customer, such as a data center or a large factory, that draws tens of megawatts or more; utilities and grid operators set their own thresholds.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f08-large-loads.html">F8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="large-load-tariff" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-large-load-tariff">
<h3 id="glossary-name-large-load-tariff"><a href="#large-load-tariff">Large-load tariff</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A tariff for very large new customers, such as data centers or factories, with terms such as minimum bills, long contracts and exit fees that can reduce other customers&#x27; exposure if the load uses less than it promised.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a04-retail-tariffs.html">A4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="lateral" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-lateral">
<h3 id="glossary-name-lateral"><a href="#lateral">Lateral</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A side branch of a distribution feeder that serves one street or block, often protected by its own fuse.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="latin-hypercube" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-latin-hypercube">
<h3 id="glossary-name-latin-hypercube"><a href="#latin-hypercube">Latin hypercube sampling</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A way to draw many sets of uncertain inputs so that the whole range of every input is covered evenly.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf7-cost-of-waiting.html">CF7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="lbnl" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-lbnl">
<h3 id="glossary-name-lbnl"><a href="#lbnl">LBNL</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, a laboratory of the United States Department of Energy that publishes, among other datasets, a yearly one of the projects waiting in interconnection queues across the country.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf3-hydrogen-under-uncertainty.html">CF3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="least-cost-path" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-least-cost-path">
<h3 id="glossary-name-least-cost-path"><a href="#least-cost-path">Least-cost path</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The route between two places across a cost surface whose summed costs are the lowest.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a19-gis-siting.html">A19</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="length-scale" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-length-scale">
<h3 id="glossary-name-length-scale"><a href="#length-scale">Length-scale</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">In a Gaussian process, how far along the input one point&#x27;s influence reaches: short length-scales give wiggly fits, long ones stiff fits.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m09-surrogates-uq.html">M9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="lcoe" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-lcoe">
<h3 id="glossary-name-lcoe"><a href="#lcoe">Levelized cost of electricity (LCOE)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A plant&#x27;s lifetime costs divided by the electricity it makes over its life, both discounted to today&#x27;s money, giving an average cost per megawatt-hour.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="07-cost.html">lesson 7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="lcoh" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-lcoh">
<h3 id="glossary-name-lcoh"><a href="#lcoh">Levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The cost of making one kilogram of hydrogen over a plant&#x27;s life: discounted lifetime costs divided by discounted lifetime kilograms (with the same cost and output every year, one year&#x27;s annualized cost divided by one year&#x27;s kilograms, as in CF2&#x27;s toy).</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.html">CF2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="life-cycle-assessment" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-life-cycle-assessment">
<h3 id="glossary-name-life-cycle-assessment"><a href="#life-cycle-assessment">Life cycle assessment (LCA)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Counting a product&#x27;s environmental effects, such as CO₂ emissions or water use, over its whole life, from materials to disposal.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r10-question-studio.html">R10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="life-cycle-cost" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-life-cycle-cost">
<h3 id="glossary-name-life-cycle-cost"><a href="#life-cycle-cost">Life-cycle cost</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Everything a system costs over its whole life, building, running, repairs and replacements, in today&#x27;s money.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.html">CF2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="linear-program" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-linear-program">
<h3 id="glossary-name-linear-program"><a href="#linear-program">Linear program</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An optimization problem in which the goal and all the rules are linear, so each is a sum of quantities times fixed numbers.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="10-write-it-down.html">lesson 10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="linear-regression" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-linear-regression">
<h3 id="glossary-name-linear-regression"><a href="#linear-regression">Linear regression</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A model that predicts a quantity as a weighted sum of inputs, with the weights chosen to make the squared misses on past data as small as possible.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m10-ml-forecasting.html">M10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="linearized-feeder-limit" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-linearized-feeder-limit">
<h3 id="glossary-name-linearized-feeder-limit"><a href="#linearized-feeder-limit">Linearized feeder limit</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A ceiling on the power through a substation or feeder in each hour, written as a straight-line rule a linear program can use, with no voltage or power-flow physics.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="sb3-city-planner.html">SB3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="lng" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-lng">
<h3 id="glossary-name-lng"><a href="#lng">Liquefied natural gas (LNG)</a></h3>
