<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Natural gas cooled until it turns liquid, so that ships can carry it across oceans; it is warmed back into gas where it lands.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="x02-fossil-transition.html">X2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="load-factor" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-load-factor">
<h3 id="glossary-name-load-factor"><a href="#load-factor">Load factor</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Average demand over a period divided by the peak demand in that period.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="02-demand.html">lesson 2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="load-relief" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-load-relief">
<h3 id="glossary-name-load-relief"><a href="#load-relief">Load relief</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The small drop in demand when the frequency falls, because many motors turn a little slower and draw less power.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="03-balancing.html">lesson 3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="load-duration-curve" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-load-duration-curve">
<h3 id="glossary-name-load-duration-curve"><a href="#load-duration-curve">Load-duration curve</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A year&#x27;s hourly demand sorted from highest to lowest, showing for how many hours each level of demand is needed.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="02-demand.html">lesson 2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="location-based" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-location-based">
<h3 id="glossary-name-location-based"><a href="#location-based">Location-based method</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A way to report electricity&#x27;s emissions that counts each MWh at the average emission factor of the grid where it is used.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a10-emissions-questions.html">A10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="locational-marginal-price" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-locational-marginal-price">
<h3 id="glossary-name-locational-marginal-price"><a href="#locational-marginal-price">Locational marginal price (LMP)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The extra cost per megawatt-hour of serving a small increase in demand at one place on the grid in one interval, given the plants running and the limits of the lines.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m01-dispatch-to-lmp.html">M1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="lock-file" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-lock-file">
<h3 id="glossary-name-lock-file"><a href="#lock-file">Lock file</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A file in a repository that pins the exact version of every package the code uses, so the same environment can be built again.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="lock-in" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-lock-in">
<h3 id="glossary-name-lock-in"><a href="#lock-in">Lock-in</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">When long-lived plants, pipes and habits keep a fuel in use for decades after they are built, because leaving them early is costly.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="x02-fossil-transition.html">X2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="log-scale" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-log-scale">
<h3 id="glossary-name-log-scale"><a href="#log-scale">Log scale</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A scale on which each equal step multiplies the value by the same factor, often 10, so tiny and huge values fit on one chart.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="01-power-energy.html">lesson 1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="logistics-cost" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-logistics-cost">
<h3 id="glossary-name-logistics-cost"><a href="#logistics-cost">Logistics cost</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The cost of moving and storing goods between factories, warehouses and stores: shipping, warehousing and handling.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf1-supply-chain-microgrids.html">CF1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="long-duration-storage" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-long-duration-storage">
<h3 id="glossary-name-long-duration-storage"><a href="#long-duration-storage">Long-duration storage</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Storage for extended discharge, including the Department of Energy&#x27;s 2023 inter-day (10–36 hours) and multi-day or week-long (36–160 hours) categories, though definitions vary.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-source">Source: <a href="https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2023-08/Pathways%20to%20Commercial%20Liftoff%20Long%20Duration%20Energy%20Storage%20Opportunities.pdf#page=13">Department of Energy, Long Duration Energy Storage Opportunities (July 27, 2023), slide 13</a></p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a08-storage-duration.html">A8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="lole" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-lole">
<h3 id="glossary-name-lole"><a href="#lole">Loss-of-load expectation (LOLE)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The expected number of days a year on which supply falls short of demand at least once, of any size or length, averaged over many simulated years; an expectation, not a count of real outages.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m03-capacity-expansion.html">M3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="lolh" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-lolh">
<h3 id="glossary-name-lolh"><a href="#lolh">Loss-of-load hours (LOLH)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The expected number of hours a year in which supply falls short of demand, averaged over many simulated years.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a05-adequacy.html">A5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="lower-bound" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-lower-bound">
<h3 id="glossary-name-lower-bound"><a href="#lower-bound">Lower bound</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A value the best answer cannot fall below; in a cost-minimizing model, the cost of a relaxation is one.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m02-unit-commitment.html">M2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="lower-heating-value" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-lower-heating-value">
<h3 id="glossary-name-lower-heating-value"><a href="#lower-heating-value">Lower heating value</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The heat a fuel gives when it burns, not counting the extra heat won by condensing the water vapor it makes; for hydrogen, about 33 kWh per kg.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a16-hydrogen-ptx.html">A16</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="lp-relaxation" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-lp-relaxation">
<h3 id="glossary-name-lp-relaxation"><a href="#lp-relaxation">LP relaxation</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The same model with every whole-number decision allowed to take any value in between, such as a switch anywhere from 0 to 1; its best cost is a lower bound for the real model.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m02-unit-commitment.html">M2</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-m" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-m">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-m">M</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="major-event-day" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-major-event-day">
<h3 id="glossary-name-major-event-day"><a href="#major-event-day">Major event day</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A day whose outage minutes per customer pass a threshold set from a utility&#x27;s past five years of daily values (IEEE 1366), often in severe weather; reports give reliability with and without them.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="managed-charging" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-managed-charging">
<h3 id="glossary-name-managed-charging"><a href="#managed-charging">Managed charging</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Charging electric cars in the hours a utility or an aggregator chooses, within limits the drivers set, instead of as soon as they plug in.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="sb3-city-planner.html">SB3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="margin" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-margin">
<h3 id="glossary-name-margin"><a href="#margin">Margin</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">What a business earns from its output after paying its operating costs: revenue minus operating costs.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf7-cost-of-waiting.html">CF7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="benchmark-margin" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-benchmark-margin">
<h3 id="glossary-name-benchmark-margin"><a href="#benchmark-margin">Margin against a benchmark</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How much cheaper or dearer an option is than a benchmark, such as buying all power from the grid.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf5-drawing-the-boundary.html">CF5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="marginal-abatement-cost-curve" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-marginal-abatement-cost-curve">
<h3 id="glossary-name-marginal-abatement-cost-curve"><a href="#marginal-abatement-cost-curve">Marginal abatement cost curve</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A chart of measures that cut emissions, each a bar as wide as the tonnes it avoids and as high as its cost per tonne, sorted cheapest first.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a18-city-plan.html">A18</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="marginal-cost" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-marginal-cost">
<h3 id="glossary-name-marginal-cost"><a href="#marginal-cost">Marginal cost</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">What one more unit costs, here the extra running cost of one more megawatt-hour of demand.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="09-storage.html">lesson 9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="marginal-emission-factor" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-marginal-emission-factor">
<h3 id="glossary-name-marginal-emission-factor"><a href="#marginal-emission-factor">Marginal emission factor</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The change in a grid&#x27;s total CO₂ caused by a small change in electricity demand; in Prairie Town, the CO₂ rate of the next plant that responds.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf6-shifting-load-to-clean-hours.html">CF6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="marginal-plant" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-marginal-plant">
<h3 id="glossary-name-marginal-plant"><a href="#marginal-plant">Marginal plant</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The plant that serves the last megawatt of demand, whose offer sets the clearing price.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="08-merit-order.html">lesson 8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="market-coupling" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-market-coupling">
<h3 id="glossary-name-market-coupling"><a href="#market-coupling">Market coupling</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Joining neighboring power markets so that one calculation sets their prices and the flows between them, sending power toward higher prices until the links are full.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="market-based" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-market-based">
<h3 id="glossary-name-market-based"><a href="#market-based">Market-based method</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A way to report electricity&#x27;s emissions that counts each MWh at the factor of the electricity the buyer purchased, through contracts or certificates.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a10-emissions-questions.html">A10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="matched-comparison" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-matched-comparison">
<h3 id="glossary-name-matched-comparison"><a href="#matched-comparison">Matched comparison</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A comparison that pairs each unit that got the change with one that did not but was similar before it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m14-did-it-work.html">M14</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="matrix" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-matrix">
<h3 id="glossary-name-matrix"><a href="#matrix">Matrix</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A table of numbers in rows and columns; in a model, one row per rule and one column per decision.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k06-vectors-matrices.html">K6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="maximum-likelihood" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-maximum-likelihood">
<h3 id="glossary-name-maximum-likelihood"><a href="#maximum-likelihood">Maximum likelihood</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Choosing a model&#x27;s settings so that the data actually observed are as probable as possible under the model.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m09-surrogates-uq.html">M9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="mcda" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-mcda">
<h3 id="glossary-name-mcda"><a href="#mcda">MCDA (multi-criteria decision analysis)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Scoring options against several goals at once, such as cost, emissions and fairness, with weights that the people deciding set.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r10-question-studio.html">R10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="mean" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-mean">
<h3 id="glossary-name-mean"><a href="#mean">Mean</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The average of a set of values: their sum divided by how many there are.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k05-probability-statistics.html">K5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="mae" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-mae">
<h3 id="glossary-name-mae"><a href="#mae">Mean absolute error (MAE)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The average size of a forecast&#x27;s misses, in the units of what is forecast, ignoring whether they were too high or too low.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="04-forecasts.html">lesson 4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="mape" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-mape">
<h3 id="glossary-name-mape"><a href="#mape">Mean absolute percentage error (MAPE)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The average miss as a percentage of the actual value; it breaks down when actual values are near zero.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="04-forecasts.html">lesson 4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="median" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-median">
<h3 id="glossary-name-median"><a href="#median">Median</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The middle value of a set sorted from lowest to highest: half the values lie below it, half above.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="b02-python-data.html">B2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="medoid" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-medoid">
<h3 id="glossary-name-medoid"><a href="#medoid">Medoid</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The member of a group whose total distance to the other members is smallest; unlike an average, it is a real member.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m03-capacity-expansion.html">M3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="megapascal" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-megapascal">
<h3 id="glossary-name-megapascal"><a href="#megapascal">Megapascal (MPa)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A unit of pressure, one million pascals; the air pressure at sea level is about 0.1 MPa.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="megawatt" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-megawatt">
<h3 id="glossary-name-megawatt"><a href="#megawatt">Megawatt (MW)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A unit of power equal to one million watts, or a thousand kilowatts.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="00-grid-operator.html">lesson 0</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="megawatt-hour" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-megawatt-hour">
<h3 id="glossary-name-megawatt-hour"><a href="#megawatt-hour">Megawatt-hour (MWh)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A unit of energy: one megawatt kept up for one hour, or a thousand kilowatt-hours.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="00-grid-operator.html">lesson 0</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="merchant-generator" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-merchant-generator">
<h3 id="glossary-name-merchant-generator"><a href="#merchant-generator">Merchant generator</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A power plant that sells its output into the wholesale market at whatever prices it fetches, rather than to one customer under a fixed arrangement.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf5-drawing-the-boundary.html">CF5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="merge" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-merge">
<h3 id="glossary-name-merge"><a href="#merge">Merge</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Combining two lines of commits, with conflicting changes requiring resolution before the merge is complete.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="merit-order" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-merit-order">
<h3 id="glossary-name-merit-order"><a href="#merit-order">Merit order</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Running power plants in order of their running cost, cheapest first.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="00-grid-operator.html">lesson 0</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="meshed-network" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-meshed-network">
<h3 id="glossary-name-meshed-network"><a href="#meshed-network">Meshed network</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A network with loops, so power can reach a place by more than one path, as transmission networks do.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="methane-leak" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-methane-leak">
<h3 id="glossary-name-methane-leak"><a href="#methane-leak">Methane leak</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Natural gas that escapes from wells, pipes, compressors and tanks before it is burned; it is mostly methane, a strong warming gas.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f11-air-climate-people.html">F11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="method-family" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-method-family">
<h3 id="glossary-name-method-family"><a href="#method-family">Method family</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A group of research methods that answer the same kind of question in a similar way, such as optimization, simulation or statistics.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r03-system-and-method.html">R3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="microgrid" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-microgrid">
<h3 id="glossary-name-microgrid"><a href="#microgrid">Microgrid</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Loads and sources inside one electrical boundary, such as a campus or a village, run as one system; a grid-connected microgrid can disconnect and run alone, and an isolated one always does.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f01-five-scales.html">F1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="mini-grid" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-mini-grid">
<h3 id="glossary-name-mini-grid"><a href="#mini-grid">Mini-grid</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A small local grid, with its own sources, storage and wires, that serves a village or a town that the main grid does not reach.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a14-microgrid-value.html">A14</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="minimum-billing-demand" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-minimum-billing-demand">
<h3 id="glossary-name-minimum-billing-demand"><a href="#minimum-billing-demand">Minimum billing demand</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The least demand, often a share of the contracted kW or MW, that a customer is billed for each month however low its demand.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a04-retail-tariffs.html">A4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="minimum-down-time" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-minimum-down-time">
<h3 id="glossary-name-minimum-down-time"><a href="#minimum-down-time">Minimum down time</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The hours a plant must stay off once stopped before it may start again.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m02-unit-commitment.html">M2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="minimum-load" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-minimum-load">
<h3 id="glossary-name-minimum-load"><a href="#minimum-load">Minimum load</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The lowest output at which a machine can keep running; below it the machine must stop, such as an electrolyzer below a set share of its size.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a16-hydrogen-ptx.html">A16</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="minimum-run-time" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-minimum-run-time">
<h3 id="glossary-name-minimum-run-time"><a href="#minimum-run-time">Minimum run time</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The hours a plant must stay on once started; the minimum down time is the hours it must stay off once stopped.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m02-unit-commitment.html">M2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="minimum-stable-output" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-minimum-stable-output">
<h3 id="glossary-name-minimum-stable-output"><a href="#minimum-stable-output">Minimum stable output</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The lowest output at which a running plant can operate steadily; below it the plant must switch off.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m02-unit-commitment.html">M2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="minimum-up-down-time" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-minimum-up-down-time">
<h3 id="glossary-name-minimum-up-down-time"><a href="#minimum-up-down-time">Minimum up and down times</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The shortest time a unit must stay on once started, and off once stopped, before it may switch again.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf4-existing-reactors-hydrogen.html">CF4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="missing-money" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-missing-money">
<h3 id="glossary-name-missing-money"><a href="#missing-money">Missing money</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The gap between what a plant the grid needs earns from energy and reserves and what it costs to build or keep.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a03-market-design.html">A3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="mixed-integer-program" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-mixed-integer-program">
<h3 id="glossary-name-mixed-integer-program"><a href="#mixed-integer-program">Mixed-integer program</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An optimization model in which some decisions must be whole numbers, such as a plant being on (1) or off (0).</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="11-solver.html">lesson 11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="mmbtu" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-mmbtu">
<h3 id="glossary-name-mmbtu"><a href="#mmbtu">MMBtu</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">One million British thermal units, a unit of fuel heat; about 0.29 MWh of heat, and gas is priced in dollars per MMBtu.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="07-cost.html">lesson 7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="moderator" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-moderator">
<h3 id="glossary-name-moderator"><a href="#moderator">Moderator</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A material, such as ordinary water or graphite, that slows the fast neutrons from fission so that uranium-235 captures them more easily.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="monte-carlo" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-monte-carlo">
<h3 id="glossary-name-monte-carlo"><a href="#monte-carlo">Monte Carlo</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A method that runs a calculation many times on randomly drawn inputs and reads the spread of the results.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k05-probability-statistics.html">K5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="monte-carlo-error" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-monte-carlo-error">
<h3 id="glossary-name-monte-carlo-error"><a href="#monte-carlo-error">Monte Carlo error</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How far an estimate from a Monte Carlo study would move with another random seed; it shrinks roughly with the square root of the number of runs.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m07-monte-carlo.html">M7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="multi-fidelity" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-multi-fidelity">
<h3 id="glossary-name-multi-fidelity"><a href="#multi-fidelity">Multi-fidelity data</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A cheap, approximate source of data combined with a few costly, accurate ones, so the cheap one fills the gaps between them.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m09-surrogates-uq.html">M9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="multi-objective" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-multi-objective">
<h3 id="glossary-name-multi-objective"><a href="#multi-objective">Multi-objective problem</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A choice with several goals that cannot all be at their best at once.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a22-tradeoff-explorer.html">A22</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="multiplication-factor" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-multiplication-factor">
<h3 id="glossary-name-multiplication-factor"><a href="#multiplication-factor">Multiplication factor (k)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">In a chain reaction, the number of new fissions each fission leads to on average: below 1 the chain dies out, at 1 it holds steady, above 1 it grows.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="must-run" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-must-run">
<h3 id="glossary-name-must-run"><a href="#must-run">Must-run rule</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A rule that keeps a plant running at or above a set output whatever the price, for example because it cannot stop and restart quickly.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a10-emissions-questions.html">A10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="mw-it" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-mw-it">
<h3 id="glossary-name-mw-it"><a href="#mw-it">MW-IT</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Megawatts of a data center&#x27;s computing equipment; the grid must supply more, for cooling and the rest of the building.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf7-cost-of-waiting.html">CF7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="mwt-mwe" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-mwt-mwe">
<h3 id="glossary-name-mwt-mwe"><a href="#mwt-mwe">MWt and MWe</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Megawatts of heat (thermal) and megawatts of electricity (electric); a plant&#x27;s MWe is its MWt times its efficiency.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-n" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-n">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-n">N</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="nacelle" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-nacelle">
<h3 id="glossary-name-nacelle"><a href="#nacelle">Nacelle</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The equipment housing on top of a wind turbine&#x27;s tower, holding the gearbox and generator that the rotor turns.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="nadir" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-nadir">
<h3 id="glossary-name-nadir"><a href="#nadir">Nadir</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The lowest point the frequency reaches after a power plant trips, before it starts to recover.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="03-balancing.html">lesson 3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="negative-control" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-negative-control">
<h3 id="glossary-name-negative-control"><a href="#negative-control">Negative control</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A test run in which the method should find nothing, for example inputs with no real signal, to show that a result is not an artifact of the method.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf8-power-curves-from-scarce-data.html">CF8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="negative-price" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-negative-price">
<h3 id="glossary-name-negative-price"><a href="#negative-price">Negative price</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A wholesale price below zero, which happens when the last plant needed would rather pay than stop running.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="08-merit-order.html">lesson 8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="net-billing" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-net-billing">
<h3 id="glossary-name-net-billing"><a href="#net-billing">Net billing</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A billing rule under which kWh sent back to the grid earn a credit set separately from the retail price, often the value of energy in that hour.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a04-retail-tariffs.html">A4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="net-calorific-value" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-net-calorific-value">
<h3 id="glossary-name-net-calorific-value"><a href="#net-calorific-value">Net calorific value</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The heat a fuel gives when burned, not counting the heat in the water vapor it forms; it is a little lower than the gross value.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f11-air-climate-people.html">F11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="net-demand" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-net-demand">
<h3 id="glossary-name-net-demand"><a href="#net-demand">Net demand (net load)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Demand left after subtracting wind and solar output; other generation, storage, imports or lower demand must cover it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="02-demand.html">lesson 2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="net-jobs" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-net-jobs">
<h3 id="glossary-name-net-jobs"><a href="#net-jobs">Net jobs</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Jobs created minus jobs lost and minus work that would have existed anyway, so the change a project really makes.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a13-fairness-jobs.html">A13</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="net-metering" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-net-metering">
<h3 id="glossary-name-net-metering"><a href="#net-metering">Net metering</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A billing rule under which each kWh a customer sends back to the grid earns the same price as a kWh it buys.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a04-retail-tariffs.html">A4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="net-present-value" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-net-present-value">
<h3 id="glossary-name-net-present-value"><a href="#net-present-value">Net present value</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The present value of a project&#x27;s future income minus the present value of its costs; above zero, it earns more than it costs at the chosen discount rate.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r10-question-studio.html">R10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="net-zero" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-net-zero">
<h3 id="glossary-name-net-zero"><a href="#net-zero">Net zero (CO₂)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The point at which the CO₂ a country or the world adds to the air each year is balanced by the CO₂ it removes, so that cumulative emissions stop rising.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f02-systems-and-map.html">F2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="net-benefit-test" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-net-benefit-test">
<h3 id="glossary-name-net-benefit-test"><a href="#net-benefit-test">Net-benefit test</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A check that an option&#x27;s total benefits across all affected parties exceed its total costs, each counted once.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf7-cost-of-waiting.html">CF7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="network-upgrade" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-network-upgrade">
<h3 id="glossary-name-network-upgrade"><a href="#network-upgrade">Network upgrade</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">New or stronger lines, transformers or substation equipment that the grid needs before a project can connect.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a06-interconnection.html">A6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="neutral" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-neutral">
<h3 id="glossary-name-neutral"><a href="#neutral">Neutral</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The grounded wire from a service transformer&#x27;s midpoint: a home gets 120 V between it and either live wire, and 240 V between the two live wires.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="neutron" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-neutron">
<h3 id="glossary-name-neutron"><a href="#neutron">Neutron</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A particle with no electric charge in the nucleus of an atom; in a reactor, the neutrons from one fission go on to split more atoms.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="no-load-cost" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-no-load-cost">
<h3 id="glossary-name-no-load-cost"><a href="#no-load-cost">No-load cost</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">What a plant costs for each hour it is on, before it makes any power.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m02-unit-commitment.html">M2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="nominal-rate" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-nominal-rate">
<h3 id="glossary-name-nominal-rate"><a href="#nominal-rate">Nominal rate</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An interest or discount rate that includes inflation, used with cash counted in the dollars of each future year.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k03-discounting.html">K3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="non-energy-use" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-non-energy-use">
<h3 id="glossary-name-non-energy-use"><a href="#non-energy-use">Non-energy use</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Fuels used as raw materials rather than burned for energy, such as natural gas for fertilizer or oil for plastics and asphalt.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="normal-distribution" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-normal-distribution">
<h3 id="glossary-name-normal-distribution"><a href="#normal-distribution">Normal distribution</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A symmetric, bell-shaped spread of values set by its mean and standard deviation, also called Gaussian; about 68% of its values lie within one standard deviation of the mean.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k05-probability-statistics.html">K5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="notebook" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-notebook">
<h3 id="glossary-name-notebook"><a href="#notebook">Notebook</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A document of code cells and text, such as a Jupyter notebook: you run each cell on its own, and its output appears under it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="notebook-kernel" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-notebook-kernel">
<h3 id="glossary-name-notebook-kernel"><a href="#notebook-kernel">Notebook kernel</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The running program behind a notebook that holds its variables in memory between cells, whatever order the cells were run in.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="n-minus-one" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-n-minus-one">
<h3 id="glossary-name-n-minus-one"><a href="#n-minus-one">N−1</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A planning rule: after any one element, such as a line, fails, the system keeps serving its customers with every remaining part within its limits.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-o" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-o">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-o">O</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="objective" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-objective">
<h3 id="glossary-name-objective"><a href="#objective">Objective</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">What an optimization tries to make as small or as large as possible, such as the total cost.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="10-write-it-down.html">lesson 10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="offer-cap" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-offer-cap">
<h3 id="glossary-name-offer-cap"><a href="#offer-cap">Offer cap</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The highest price a market&#x27;s rules let a seller put in an offer; clearing prices can still rise above it, for example through scarcity pricing or congestion.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a03-market-design.html">A3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="operating-emissions" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-operating-emissions">
<h3 id="glossary-name-operating-emissions"><a href="#operating-emissions">Operating emissions</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The CO2 released where fuel is burned to make electricity, leaving out building the plant and producing and delivering its fuel.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="00-grid-operator.html">lesson 0</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="optimality-gap" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-optimality-gap">
<h3 id="glossary-name-optimality-gap"><a href="#optimality-gap">Optimality gap</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">For a mixed-integer program, the remaining distance between the best plan the solver has found and the bound it has proven, so 0% means proven best.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="11-solver.html">lesson 11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="optimization" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-optimization">
<h3 id="glossary-name-optimization"><a href="#optimization">Optimization</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Finding the best choice among many, given a goal and the rules the choice must obey.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="10-write-it-down.html">lesson 10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="optimization-window" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-optimization-window">
<h3 id="glossary-name-optimization-window"><a href="#optimization-window">Optimization window</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The stretch of time, such as a month, within which a model may move electricity use between hours while keeping the total over that stretch.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf6-shifting-load-to-clean-hours.html">CF6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="order-of-magnitude" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-order-of-magnitude">
<h3 id="glossary-name-order-of-magnitude"><a href="#order-of-magnitude">Order of magnitude</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The power of ten nearest a quantity on a log scale, where a leading number from √10 ≈ 3.16 up rounds to the next power; two quantities are an order of magnitude apart when one is about ten times the other.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k01-units.html">K1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="outlet-temperature" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-outlet-temperature">
<h3 id="glossary-name-outlet-temperature"><a href="#outlet-temperature">Outlet temperature</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The temperature of the coolant as it leaves a reactor core; it sets how hot the heat is that a plant can supply.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="overnight-cost" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-overnight-cost">
<h3 id="glossary-name-overnight-cost"><a href="#overnight-cost">Overnight cost</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The cost to build a power plant as if it were built overnight, so with no interest paid during construction, usually given per kilowatt.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="07-cost.html">lesson 7</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-p" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-p">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-p">P</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="parallel-trends" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-parallel-trends">
<h3 id="glossary-name-parallel-trends"><a href="#parallel-trends">Parallel trends</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The assumption behind difference-in-differences: without the program, the treated and comparison groups would have changed by the same amount.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m14-did-it-work.html">M14</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="parameter" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-parameter">
<h3 id="glossary-name-parameter"><a href="#parameter">Parameter</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A number a model is given and takes as it is, such as demand or a plant&#x27;s running cost, as opposed to a decision it makes.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="10-write-it-down.html">lesson 10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="pareto-frontier" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-pareto-frontier">
<h3 id="glossary-name-pareto-frontier"><a href="#pareto-frontier">Pareto frontier</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The set of plans that cannot be made cheaper without becoming dirtier, or cleaner without becoming more expensive.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="12-trade-offs.html">lesson 12</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="part-load-efficiency" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-part-load-efficiency">
<h3 id="glossary-name-part-load-efficiency"><a href="#part-load-efficiency">Part-load efficiency</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How well a machine converts energy when it runs below its full size; many chillers and turbines do worse at part load.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf5-drawing-the-boundary.html">CF5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="participatory-mapping" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-participatory-mapping">
<h3 id="glossary-name-participatory-mapping"><a href="#participatory-mapping">Participatory mapping</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A method in which residents mark on maps the places that matter to them, for planners to weigh.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="x06-social-methods.html">X6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="passive-safety" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-passive-safety">
<h3 id="glossary-name-passive-safety"><a href="#passive-safety">Passive safety</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Safety features that rely on natural effects, such as hot fluid rising and cool fluid sinking, instead of pumps, outside power or operators.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="payback-period" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-payback-period">
<h3 id="glossary-name-payback-period"><a href="#payback-period">Payback period</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The number of years until the running sum of a project&#x27;s cash first gets back to zero, with or without discounting.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a01-project-tea.html">A1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="peak-demand" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-peak-demand">
<h3 id="glossary-name-peak-demand"><a href="#peak-demand">Peak demand</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The highest demand in a period, such as the busiest hour of a year; the grid must be able to meet it, with a margin.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="02-demand.html">lesson 2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="peaker" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-peaker">
<h3 id="glossary-name-peaker"><a href="#peaker">Peaker</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A power plant that runs only in the hours of highest demand, because it starts quickly but is expensive to run.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="00-grid-operator.html">lesson 0</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="pem-electrolyzer" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-pem-electrolyzer">
<h3 id="glossary-name-pem-electrolyzer"><a href="#pem-electrolyzer">PEM electrolyzer</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An electrolyzer that uses a proton exchange membrane to carry ions between its electrodes, with operating limits that depend on the equipment design.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a16-hydrogen-ptx.html">A16</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="penalty" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-penalty">
<h3 id="glossary-name-penalty"><a href="#penalty">Penalty</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An extra cost added to a model&#x27;s objective for an action it should not take too freely, such as adjusting an hour&#x27;s load.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf6-shifting-load-to-clean-hours.html">CF6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="penstock" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-penstock">
<h3 id="glossary-name-penstock"><a href="#penstock">Penstock</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The large pipe that carries water down from a reservoir to a hydro plant&#x27;s turbine.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="per-unit" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-per-unit">
<h3 id="glossary-name-per-unit"><a href="#per-unit">Per unit</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A voltage written as a fraction of its nominal value: 1.00 per unit is 120 V on a 120 V service, 0.95 is 114 V.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a17-physical-feasibility.html">A17</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="percentile" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-percentile">
<h3 id="glossary-name-percentile"><a href="#percentile">Percentile</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The value that a given share of a sorted set stays at or below: 90% of values are at or below the 90th percentile.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k05-probability-statistics.html">K5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="perfect-foresight" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-perfect-foresight">
<h3 id="glossary-name-perfect-foresight"><a href="#perfect-foresight">Perfect foresight</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A model assumption that every future value in the horizon, such as tomorrow&#x27;s demand and weather, is known when decisions are made; it gives an upper bound on how much flexibility can cut a model&#x27;s running cost.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r05-build-validate.html">R5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="period-weight" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-period-weight">
<h3 id="glossary-name-period-weight"><a href="#period-weight">Period weight</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How many hours of the year one modeled hour of a representative period stands for; a model multiplies that hour&#x27;s running cost and emissions by it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m03-capacity-expansion.html">M3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="persistence-forecast" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-persistence-forecast">
<h3 id="glossary-name-persistence-forecast"><a href="#persistence-forecast">Persistence forecast</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The simplest forecast: the next value will be the same as the last one seen, or as the same hour a day or a week before.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="04-forecasts.html">lesson 4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="petajoule" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-petajoule">
<h3 id="glossary-name-petajoule"><a href="#petajoule">Petajoule (PJ)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A unit of energy equal to a million gigajoules (10^15 joules, about 278 GWh), used for a country&#x27;s yearly fuel use.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a21-security-minerals.html">A21</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="photovoltaic" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-photovoltaic">
<h3 id="glossary-name-photovoltaic"><a href="#photovoltaic">Photovoltaic (PV)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Solar panels that turn sunlight directly into electricity.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.html">CF2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="physical-energy-content" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-physical-energy-content">
<h3 id="glossary-name-physical-energy-content"><a href="#physical-energy-content">Physical energy content method</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A rule for counting primary energy in which nuclear power counts as the heat its reactors make and hydro, wind and solar as the electricity they make; the IEA and Eurostat use it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="piecewise-linear" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-piecewise-linear">
<h3 id="glossary-name-piecewise-linear"><a href="#piecewise-linear">Piecewise-linear curve</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A curve drawn as straight pieces joined end to end, so a linear or mixed-integer program can follow it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf4-existing-reactors-hydrogen.html">CF4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="pinball-loss" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-pinball-loss">
<h3 id="glossary-name-pinball-loss"><a href="#pinball-loss">Pinball loss</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The score of a percentile forecast: a 90th-percentile forecast should sit above about 90% of outcomes, so an outcome above it costs 0.9 times the miss and one below it 0.1 times; lower is better.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m09-surrogates-uq.html">M9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="placed-in-service" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-placed-in-service">
<h3 id="glossary-name-placed-in-service"><a href="#placed-in-service">Placed in service</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The date a facility is ready and available to do its job; many tax credits start their clock on it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m11-tea-in-models.html">M11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="point-of-common-coupling" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-point-of-common-coupling">
<h3 id="glossary-name-point-of-common-coupling"><a href="#point-of-common-coupling">Point of common coupling</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The place where a grid-connected microgrid meets the main grid, with the switch that opens to let it run on its own.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f07-microgrids.html">F7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="power" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-power">
<h3 id="glossary-name-power"><a href="#power">Power</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How fast electricity is being made or used at a given moment, measured in watts, kilowatts (kW) or megawatts (MW).</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="00-grid-operator.html">lesson 0</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="power-coefficient" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-power-coefficient">
<h3 id="glossary-name-power-coefficient"><a href="#power-coefficient">Power coefficient (Cp)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The share of the wind&#x27;s power that a turbine turns into electricity; no rotor can capture more than 16/27, about 59% (the Betz limit).</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="05-capacity-factor.html">lesson 5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="power-curve" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-power-curve">
<h3 id="glossary-name-power-curve"><a href="#power-curve">Power curve</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A chart of how much power a wind turbine makes at each wind speed.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="05-capacity-factor.html">lesson 5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="power-factor" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-power-factor">
<h3 id="glossary-name-power-factor"><a href="#power-factor">Power factor</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Real power divided by apparent power, MW ÷ MVA: 1 when no reactive power flows, lower as more does.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a17-physical-feasibility.html">A17</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="power-purchase-agreement" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-power-purchase-agreement">
<h3 id="glossary-name-power-purchase-agreement"><a href="#power-purchase-agreement">Power purchase agreement (PPA)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A long contract between a power plant&#x27;s seller and a buyer that sets the price paid for the plant&#x27;s power, or for its market value.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a02-contracts-risk.html">A2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="power-usage-effectiveness" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-power-usage-effectiveness">
<h3 id="glossary-name-power-usage-effectiveness"><a href="#power-usage-effectiveness">Power usage effectiveness (PUE)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A data center&#x27;s total electricity use over a year divided by its computing equipment&#x27;s use over the same year; the rest goes to cooling, power conversion and lighting.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f08-large-loads.html">F8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="prediction-interval" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-prediction-interval">
<h3 id="glossary-name-prediction-interval"><a href="#prediction-interval">Prediction interval</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A range that should contain the actual value with a stated probability, drawn as a band around a forecast.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="04-forecasts.html">lesson 4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="present-value" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-present-value">
<h3 id="glossary-name-present-value"><a href="#present-value">Present value</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">What an amount of money paid or received in the future is worth today, once it is discounted.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="07-cost.html">lesson 7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="prevailing-wage-apprenticeship" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-prevailing-wage-apprenticeship">
<h3 id="glossary-name-prevailing-wage-apprenticeship"><a href="#prevailing-wage-apprenticeship">Prevailing wage and apprenticeship requirements</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Two federal conditions of many clean-energy tax credits, the hydrogen credit among them, that raise the credit fivefold when both are met: those who build or repair the facility are paid at least the local prevailing wage, and apprentices from registered programs work a set number of hours.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m11-tea-in-models.html">M11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="price-taker" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-price-taker">
<h3 id="glossary-name-price-taker"><a href="#price-taker">Price-taker</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A seller or buyer too small to move the market price, so a model takes the prices as given.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf4-existing-reactors-hydrogen.html">CF4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="pricing-node" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-pricing-node">
<h3 id="glossary-name-pricing-node"><a href="#pricing-node">Pricing node</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A point on the grid, such as a power plant&#x27;s connection, where the market sets its own price.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a02-contracts-risk.html">A2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="primary-energy" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-primary-energy">
<h3 id="glossary-name-primary-energy"><a href="#primary-energy">Primary energy</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Energy as found in nature before any conversion, such as the gas burned in a power plant to make the electricity a home later buys.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f03-energy-services.html">F3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="primary-response" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-primary-response">
<h3 id="glossary-name-primary-response"><a href="#primary-response">Primary frequency response</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Automatic extra output from power plants&#x27; governors within seconds of a frequency drop; it stops the fall but does not restore 60 Hz.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="03-balancing.html">lesson 3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="pro-forma" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-pro-forma">
<h3 id="glossary-name-pro-forma"><a href="#pro-forma">Pro forma rules</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A standard template of procedures, such as FERC&#x27;s for connecting generators, that each grid operator adopts with its own changes.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a06-interconnection.html">A6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="probability-distribution" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-probability-distribution">
<h3 id="glossary-name-probability-distribution"><a href="#probability-distribution">Probability distribution</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A rule that says how likely each value of an uncertain input is; a uniform distribution makes every value in its range equally likely.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m07-monte-carlo.html">M7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="process-heat" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-process-heat">
<h3 id="glossary-name-process-heat"><a href="#process-heat">Process heat</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Heat that factories use to make things, such as hot water for washing, steam for cooking and drying, or ovens and furnaces above a few hundred degrees.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a15-efficiency-electrification.html">A15</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="procurement-rule" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-procurement-rule">
<h3 id="glossary-name-procurement-rule"><a href="#procurement-rule">Procurement rule</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A rule for which purchased electricity a buyer may count as clean, for example by region, by hour and by how new the plant is; it sets a claim, not the emissions the purchase causes.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a16-hydrogen-ptx.html">A16</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="production-credit" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-production-credit">
<h3 id="glossary-name-production-credit"><a href="#production-credit">Production credit</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A payment for each megawatt-hour a plant produces, set by a policy such as a tax credit.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="08-merit-order.html">lesson 8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="productive-use" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-productive-use">
<h3 id="glossary-name-productive-use"><a href="#productive-use">Productive use</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Electricity used to earn a living, such as running a grain mill, a water pump or a cold store, rather than only for lights and phones at home.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a14-microgrid-value.html">A14</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="prognostics" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-prognostics">
<h3 id="glossary-name-prognostics"><a href="#prognostics">Prognostics</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Predicting when a machine part is likely to fail, from data on its condition, so that repairs can be planned before it does.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.html">CF2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="projection" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-projection">
<h3 id="glossary-name-projection"><a href="#projection">Projection</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A model&#x27;s estimate of a future quantity under stated assumptions, not a measurement or a promise.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="n01-news-lens.html">N1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="provenance" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-provenance">
<h3 id="glossary-name-provenance"><a href="#provenance">Provenance</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The documented origin and history of a piece of data: source, version, access date, checksums and every change made to it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r04-data.html">R4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="public-power-utility" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-public-power-utility">
<h3 id="glossary-name-public-power-utility"><a href="#public-power-utility">Public power utility</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An electric utility owned by a city or another public body, generally regulated by its own local government rather than the state commission.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f09-city-energy.html">F9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="public-utility-commission" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-public-utility-commission">
<h3 id="glossary-name-public-utility-commission"><a href="#public-utility-commission">Public utility commission</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A state&#x27;s utility regulator (in Kansas, the Kansas Corporation Commission), which sets or approves the rates and service rules of the utilities it oversees.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f09-city-energy.html">F9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="python-package" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-python-package">
<h3 id="glossary-name-python-package"><a href="#python-package">Python package</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A ready-made library of Python code, such as pandas, that a project installs with pip instead of writing it itself.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-q" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-q">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-q">Q</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="quad" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-quad">
<h3 id="glossary-name-quad"><a href="#quad">Quad</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A quadrillion (10^15) British thermal units, about 1.055 exajoules; the unit of national energy statistics in the United States.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="quartile" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-quartile">
<h3 id="glossary-name-quartile"><a href="#quartile">Quartile</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The values that cut a sorted set into four equal parts: 25% of values lie below the first, 50% below the second (the median), 75% below the third.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="b02-python-data.html">B2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="question-type" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-question-type">
<h3 id="glossary-name-question-type"><a href="#question-type">Question type</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The kind of answer a research question asks for: descriptive, explanatory, evaluative, predictive or prescriptive.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r01-framing.html">R1</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-r" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-r">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-r">R</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="radial-network" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-radial-network">
<h3 id="glossary-name-radial-network"><a href="#radial-network">Radial network</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A network shaped like a tree, with one path from the source to each customer, as most distribution feeders are.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="ramp-rate" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-ramp-rate">
<h3 id="glossary-name-ramp-rate"><a href="#ramp-rate">Ramp rate</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How fast a power plant can raise or lower its output, for example in megawatts per minute or per hour.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="00-grid-operator.html">lesson 0</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="random-seed" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-random-seed">
<h3 id="glossary-name-random-seed"><a href="#random-seed">Random seed</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A fixed starting number for a random-number generator, so a random draw comes out the same on every run.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="rank-correlation" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-rank-correlation">
<h3 id="glossary-name-rank-correlation"><a href="#rank-correlation">Rank correlation (Spearman&#x27;s ρ)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The correlation of the ranks of two quantities, from −1 to 1: how consistently one rises or falls as the other rises; it can miss U-shaped links and interactions.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m07-monte-carlo.html">M7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="raster" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-raster">
<h3 id="glossary-name-raster"><a href="#raster">Raster</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A map stored as a grid of equal cells, each holding one number or one class, such as slope or land cover.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a19-gis-siting.html">A19</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="rate-base" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-rate-base">
<h3 id="glossary-name-rate-base"><a href="#rate-base">Rate base</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The plant a regulator approves as serving customers, valued after depreciation; rates give the utility an opportunity, not a guarantee, to earn an allowed return on it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="x04-rules-law.html">X4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="rate-case" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-rate-case">
<h3 id="glossary-name-rate-case"><a href="#rate-case">Rate case</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A formal proceeding in which a utility asks its regulator to change its rates; staff, consumer advocates and other parties file testimony, and the commission decides.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="x04-rules-law.html">X4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="rocof" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-rocof">
<h3 id="glossary-name-rocof"><a href="#rocof">Rate of change of frequency</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How fast the grid&#x27;s frequency moves in the first instant after a disturbance, in hertz per second.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="03-balancing.html">lesson 3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="rated-speed" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-rated-speed">
<h3 id="glossary-name-rated-speed"><a href="#rated-speed">Rated wind speed</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The wind speed at which a turbine first reaches its full rated power; above it, the blades turn to spill the extra wind.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="05-capacity-factor.html">lesson 5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="ratepayer" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-ratepayer">
<h3 id="glossary-name-ratepayer"><a href="#ratepayer">Ratepayer</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A customer who pays a utility&#x27;s regulated electricity rates; utility costs that nobody else covers end up in those rates.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf7-cost-of-waiting.html">CF7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="reactance" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-reactance">
<h3 id="glossary-name-reactance"><a href="#reactance">Reactance</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A line&#x27;s opposition to alternating current; when several paths join two places, each carries a share of the power that falls as its reactance rises.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m01-dispatch-to-lmp.html">M1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="reactive-power" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-reactive-power">
<h3 id="glossary-name-reactive-power"><a href="#reactive-power">Reactive power</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The part of alternating-current power that flows back and forth and does no net work; supplying or absorbing it locally helps keep voltage within safe limits.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="n01-news-lens.html">N1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="real-rate" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-real-rate">
<h3 id="glossary-name-real-rate"><a href="#real-rate">Real rate</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An interest or discount rate with inflation taken out, used with costs stated in one year&#x27;s dollars.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k03-discounting.html">K3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="real-time-pricing" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-real-time-pricing">
<h3 id="glossary-name-real-time-pricing"><a href="#real-time-pricing">Real-time pricing</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A tariff whose price per kWh follows the wholesale or system price hour by hour, so the bill moves with it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a04-retail-tariffs.html">A4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="reanalysis" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-reanalysis">
<h3 id="glossary-name-reanalysis"><a href="#reanalysis">Reanalysis</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A gridded record of past weather made by running a weather model over historical observations, hour by hour for decades.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r02-literature.html">R2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="rebound-effect" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-rebound-effect">
<h3 id="glossary-name-rebound-effect"><a href="#rebound-effect">Rebound effect</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Part of an efficiency saving taken back because the cheaper service gets used more.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f02-systems-and-map.html">F2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="recloser" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-recloser">
<h3 id="glossary-name-recloser"><a href="#recloser">Recloser</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A breaker on a feeder that opens on a fault and tries closing again in seconds, so a passing fault, such as a brushing branch, causes only a blink.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="recourse" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-recourse">
<h3 id="glossary-name-recourse"><a href="#recourse">Recourse decision</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A decision made after the uncertainty resolves, such as how hard to run a plant in each branch; it can differ from branch to branch.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m08-stochastic-robust.html">M8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="refining" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-refining">
<h3 id="glossary-name-refining"><a href="#refining">Refining (of minerals)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Processing mined ore or concentrate into the pure chemicals and materials a factory can use, such as battery-grade lithium chemicals or graphite.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a21-security-minerals.html">A21</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="refuelling-outage" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-refuelling-outage">
<h3 id="glossary-name-refuelling-outage"><a href="#refuelling-outage">Refueling outage</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The planned weeks when a reactor is shut down to replace part of its fuel and carry out maintenance.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="05-capacity-factor.html">lesson 5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="rto" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-rto">
<h3 id="glossary-name-rto"><a href="#rto">Regional transmission organization (RTO)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An independent organization, such as PJM or MISO, that runs a region&#x27;s transmission grid and its wholesale electricity markets.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a03-market-design.html">A3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="regret" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-regret">
<h3 id="glossary-name-regret"><a href="#regret">Regret</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A plan&#x27;s cost in one future minus the cost of the best plan for that future, known only in hindsight; the least-regret plan keeps the largest regret smallest.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m08-stochastic-robust.html">M8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="reinforcing-loop" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-reinforcing-loop">
<h3 id="glossary-name-reinforcing-loop"><a href="#reinforcing-loop">Reinforcing loop</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A feedback loop with an even number of negative links, in which a change feeds itself, as growth or as decline.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f02-systems-and-map.html">F2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="relative-growth-index" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-relative-growth-index">
<h3 id="glossary-name-relative-growth-index"><a href="#relative-growth-index">Relative growth index (RGI)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How fast a topic&#x27;s paper count grew from 2016–18 to 2022–24, divided by the growth of energy-systems research as a whole.</p>
