<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r10-question-studio.html">R10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="renewable-penetration" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-renewable-penetration">
<h3 id="glossary-name-renewable-penetration"><a href="#renewable-penetration">Renewable penetration</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The share of a grid&#x27;s electricity that comes from wind, solar and other renewable sources.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf4-existing-reactors-hydrogen.html">CF4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="repository" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-repository">
<h3 id="glossary-name-repository"><a href="#repository">Repository</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A project folder together with its full history of commits, as kept by a version-control tool such as Git.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="representative-period" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-representative-period">
<h3 id="glossary-name-representative-period"><a href="#representative-period">Representative period</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A real stretch of time, such as a week, chosen to stand for many similar ones so that a model can run faster.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="13-capstone.html">lesson 13</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="resample" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-resample">
<h3 id="glossary-name-resample"><a href="#resample">Resample</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Regroup a time series to a coarser step, such as hours to days, by averaging or summing.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="b02-python-data.html">B2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="resampled-weather" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-resampled-weather">
<h3 id="glossary-name-resampled-weather"><a href="#resampled-weather">Resampled weather year</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A simulated year stitched together from pieces of real years, such as whole weeks, so that demand, wind and sun stay consistent within each piece; it is not an observed year.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a05-adequacy.html">A5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="research-gap" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-research-gap">
<h3 id="glossary-name-research-gap"><a href="#research-gap">Research gap</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A question the literature has not answered, shown with a logged search and the closest prior work, not just asserted.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r02-literature.html">R2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="reserve-margin" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-reserve-margin">
<h3 id="glossary-name-reserve-margin"><a href="#reserve-margin">Reserve margin</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The capacity counted as available at the peak, above the year&#x27;s peak demand, as a percentage of that peak.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a22-tradeoff-explorer.html">A22</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="reserves" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-reserves">
<h3 id="glossary-name-reserves"><a href="#reserves">Reserves</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Spare capacity that operators keep ready to cover the sudden loss of a plant or a forecast that misses.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="03-balancing.html">lesson 3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="reservoir" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-reservoir">
<h3 id="glossary-name-reservoir"><a href="#reservoir">Reservoir</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The lake a dam holds back; its water is energy stored for later, up to what it holds.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="reservoir-limit" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-reservoir-limit">
<h3 id="glossary-name-reservoir-limit"><a href="#reservoir-limit">Reservoir limit</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The lowest and highest level a store may hold, such as a tank&#x27;s minimum pressure or a reservoir&#x27;s lowest water level; a model writes it as bounds on the level.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m04-storage-multienergy.html">M4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="residual-mix" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-residual-mix">
<h3 id="glossary-name-residual-mix"><a href="#residual-mix">Residual mix</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The emission factor of the electricity left after every contract and certificate has been claimed, used for a buyer&#x27;s unclaimed use.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a10-emissions-questions.html">A10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="residual-value" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-residual-value">
<h3 id="glossary-name-residual-value"><a href="#residual-value">Residual value</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The value an asset is assumed to keep at the end of an analysis, such as the unused years of a battery bought late, counted as a credit in the last year.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="ck-a-spreadsheet.html">CK-A</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="resource-adequacy" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-resource-adequacy">
<h3 id="glossary-name-resource-adequacy"><a href="#resource-adequacy">Resource adequacy</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Whether a power system has enough supply to meet demand in nearly every hour, judged with many weather years and plant outages against a criterion such as a loss-of-load expectation.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m03-capacity-expansion.html">M3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="resource-cost" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-resource-cost">
<h3 id="glossary-name-resource-cost"><a href="#resource-cost">Resource cost</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">What a plan uses up, such as plants built, their upkeep and the fuel burned, leaving out payments that only move money between groups.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a12-policy-instruments.html">A12</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="retrofit" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-retrofit">
<h3 id="glossary-name-retrofit"><a href="#retrofit">Retrofit</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Work on an existing building, such as air sealing and insulation, that cuts the heat it needs.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="sb3-city-planner.html">SB3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="revenue-requirement" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-revenue-requirement">
<h3 id="glossary-name-revenue-requirement"><a href="#revenue-requirement">Revenue requirement</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The annual revenue a regulated utility may collect: its approved expenses, including depreciation and taxes, plus an allowed financing return on its rate base.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="x04-rules-law.html">X4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="robust-optimization" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-robust-optimization">
<h3 id="glossary-name-robust-optimization"><a href="#robust-optimization">Robust optimization</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Planning against a set of possible futures without chances: here, choosing the plan whose worst cost over the set is lowest.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m08-stochastic-robust.html">M8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="rolling-horizon" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-rolling-horizon">
<h3 id="glossary-name-rolling-horizon"><a href="#rolling-horizon">Rolling horizon</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Planning over a window ahead on a forecast, carrying out only the first hours of the plan, then planning again as the real values arrive.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m05-microgrid-size-and-run.html">M5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="rmse" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-rmse">
<h3 id="glossary-name-rmse"><a href="#rmse">Root mean square error (RMSE)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The square root of the average squared miss, in the units of the quantity; large misses count more than in the mean absolute error.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m09-surrogates-uq.html">M9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="round-trip-efficiency" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-round-trip-efficiency">
<h3 id="glossary-name-round-trip-efficiency"><a href="#round-trip-efficiency">Round-trip efficiency</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The share of the energy put into storage that comes back out.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="09-storage.html">lesson 9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="run-of-river" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-run-of-river">
<h3 id="glossary-name-run-of-river"><a href="#run-of-river">Run-of-river plant</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A hydro plant with little or no reservoir, so it makes what the river&#x27;s flow brings at the time.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="running-cost" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-running-cost">
<h3 id="glossary-name-running-cost"><a href="#running-cost">Running cost</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">What it costs a plant to make one more megawatt-hour, mostly fuel, leaving out the cost of building it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="00-grid-operator.html">lesson 0</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-s" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-s">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-s">S</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="saidi" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-saidi">
<h3 id="glossary-name-saidi"><a href="#saidi">SAIDI</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">System Average Interruption Duration Index: the minutes without power the average customer has in a year, customer-minutes divided by customers served.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="saifi" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-saifi">
<h3 id="glossary-name-saifi"><a href="#saifi">SAIFI</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">System Average Interruption Frequency Index: the number of sustained interruptions the average customer has in a year, total customer interruptions divided by customers served, so a customer interrupted twice counts twice.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="sankey-diagram" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-sankey-diagram">
<h3 id="glossary-name-sankey-diagram"><a href="#sankey-diagram">Sankey diagram</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A flow diagram in which each band&#x27;s width is the amount of energy it carries, so what flows in and out of every box can be read and compared at a glance.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="scada" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-scada">
<h3 id="glossary-name-scada"><a href="#scada">SCADA records</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The operating records a wind farm&#x27;s control system logs for each turbine, such as ten-minute averages of wind speed and power (supervisory control and data acquisition).</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m09-surrogates-uq.html">M9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="system-scale" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-system-scale">
<h3 id="glossary-name-system-scale"><a href="#system-scale">Scale (of an energy system)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A level of an energy system, from one device or plant to a whole nation, set apart by who decides what and by the physics a model of it needs.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f01-five-scales.html">F1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="scarcity-price" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-scarcity-price">
<h3 id="glossary-name-scarcity-price"><a href="#scarcity-price">Scarcity price</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A wholesale electricity price that rises when supply or operating reserves are scarce, reflecting the value of meeting demand or maintaining reserves.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f02-systems-and-map.html">F2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="scenario" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-scenario">
<h3 id="glossary-name-scenario"><a href="#scenario">Scenario</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A coherent what-if set of a model&#x27;s inputs, such as a 36-month wait; a scenario may be given a probability, though this lesson gives none.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m07-monte-carlo.html">M7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="future-scenario" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-future-scenario">
<h3 id="glossary-name-future-scenario"><a href="#future-scenario">Scenario (one possible future)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">One possible future of a model&#x27;s uncertain inputs, such as how much planned wind and solar gets built and how fast demand grows; each scenario has a chance.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf3-hydrogen-under-uncertainty.html">CF3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="scenario-tree" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-scenario-tree">
<h3 id="glossary-name-scenario-tree"><a href="#scenario-tree">Scenario tree</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A picture of a decision under uncertainty: a choice made now at the root, then one branch for each way the future may turn out, each with its chance.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m08-stochastic-robust.html">M8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="scientific-notation" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-scientific-notation">
<h3 id="glossary-name-scientific-notation"><a href="#scientific-notation">Scientific notation</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A way to write a number as a value at least 1 and less than 10, times a power of ten, so very large and very small numbers are easy to compare.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k01-units.html">K1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="scope-1" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-scope-1">
<h3 id="glossary-name-scope-1"><a href="#scope-1">Scope 1 emissions</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Emissions from sources inside the boundary being counted: a company&#x27;s own boilers and vehicles, or, for a city, fuels burned inside its border.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a18-city-plan.html">A18</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="scope-2" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-scope-2">
<h3 id="glossary-name-scope-2"><a href="#scope-2">Scope 2 emissions</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Emissions from the grid electricity, steam, heat or cooling that a company buys or a city uses, counted at the plants that make it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a10-emissions-questions.html">A10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="scope-3" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-scope-3">
<h3 id="glossary-name-scope-3"><a href="#scope-3">Scope 3 emissions</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Other emissions that happen outside the boundary because of activities inside it, such as electricity lost on the wires that bring a city its power.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a18-city-plan.html">A18</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="screening-estimate" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-screening-estimate">
<h3 id="glossary-name-screening-estimate"><a href="#screening-estimate">Screening estimate</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A quick estimate from stated assumptions and coefficients a reader can change, used to compare options, not to predict outcomes.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a13-fairness-jobs.html">A13</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="scrubber" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-scrubber">
<h3 id="glossary-name-scrubber"><a href="#scrubber">Scrubber</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Equipment that sprays a wet or dry chemical such as limestone through a plant&#x27;s exhaust to capture most of its sulfur dioxide.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f11-air-climate-people.html">F11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="sdwpf" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-sdwpf">
<h3 id="glossary-name-sdwpf"><a href="#sdwpf">SDWPF dataset</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An open dataset of one wind farm&#x27;s ten-minute operating records (SCADA), shared for research on wind power forecasting.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m09-surrogates-uq.html">M9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="search-string" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-search-string">
<h3 id="glossary-name-search-string"><a href="#search-string">Search string</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The words and operators (AND, OR, quotation marks) typed into a literature database to find papers.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r10-question-studio.html">R10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="sector-coupling" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-sector-coupling">
<h3 id="glossary-name-sector-coupling"><a href="#sector-coupling">Sector coupling</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Linking energy carriers such as electricity, hydrogen and heat through devices that convert one into another, so that one carrier&#x27;s supply and price affect the others.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m04-storage-multienergy.html">M4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="selection-bias" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-selection-bias">
<h3 id="glossary-name-selection-bias"><a href="#selection-bias">Selection bias</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A false effect from who joins: those who take up a program differ from the rest in a way the comparison does not remove (difference-in-differences removes a fixed gap, not a different trend).</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m14-did-it-work.html">M14</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="self-organizing-map" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-self-organizing-map">
<h3 id="glossary-name-self-organizing-map"><a href="#self-organizing-map">Self-organizing map</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A clustering method that places similar items, such as days, in neighboring cells of a small grid.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r02-literature.html">R2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="sensitivity-analysis" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-sensitivity-analysis">
<h3 id="glossary-name-sensitivity-analysis"><a href="#sensitivity-analysis">Sensitivity analysis</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Changing a model&#x27;s inputs one at a time and re-solving, to see which inputs the answer depends on.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="11-solver.html">lesson 11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="service-level" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-service-level">
<h3 id="glossary-name-service-level"><a href="#service-level">Service level</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The share of cases in which a rule must hold, such as meeting store demand in 95 of every 100 weeks.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m05-microgrid-size-and-run.html">M5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="service-voltage-range" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-service-voltage-range">
<h3 id="glossary-name-service-voltage-range"><a href="#service-voltage-range">Service voltage range</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The voltage a utility keeps at a customer&#x27;s meter in normal operation; in the U.S., ANSI C84.1 Range A, 114 to 126 V on a 120 V service (0.95 to 1.05 per unit).</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a17-physical-feasibility.html">A17</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="setback" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-setback">
<h3 id="glossary-name-setback"><a href="#setback">Setback</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The least distance a project must keep from a home, road, line or other feature, usually set by local rules.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a19-gis-siting.html">A19</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="settlement" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-settlement">
<h3 id="glossary-name-settlement"><a href="#settlement">Settlement (in a regulatory case)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An agreement among some or all parties to a case on how it should end, filed for the commission&#x27;s decision.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="x04-rules-law.html">X4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="shadow-price" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-shadow-price">
<h3 id="glossary-name-shadow-price"><a href="#shadow-price">Shadow price</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How much the best total cost would change if one rule were loosened by one unit; for the rule that supply equals demand, it is the price of one more megawatt-hour.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="11-solver.html">lesson 11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="sharpness" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-sharpness">
<h3 id="glossary-name-sharpness"><a href="#sharpness">Sharpness (of a forecast band)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How narrow a forecast&#x27;s bands are, on average; narrower is better only if the bands still hold what they claim.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf8-power-curves-from-scarce-data.html">CF8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="simplex-method" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-simplex-method">
<h3 id="glossary-name-simplex-method"><a href="#simplex-method">Simplex method</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A way to solve linear programs by moving from corner to neighboring corner of the feasible region, never making the goal worse, until no neighbor is better.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="11-solver.html">lesson 11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="site-control" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-site-control">
<h3 id="glossary-name-site-control"><a href="#site-control">Site control</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Proof that a project owns, leases or has the right to use the land it would be built on.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a06-interconnection.html">A6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="skill-score" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-skill-score">
<h3 id="glossary-name-skill-score"><a href="#skill-score">Skill score</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How much smaller a forecast&#x27;s error is than that of a simple baseline such as persistence.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="04-forecasts.html">lesson 4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="snowballing" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-snowballing">
<h3 id="glossary-name-snowballing"><a href="#snowballing">Snowballing</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Finding papers from one you already have: backward through its references, forward through the works that cite it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r02-literature.html">R2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="software-environment" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-software-environment">
<h3 id="glossary-name-software-environment"><a href="#software-environment">Software environment</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The language, packages and versions a program runs with, built from a lock file so that a rerun uses the same ones.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="solver" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-solver">
<h3 id="glossary-name-solver"><a href="#solver">Solver</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Software that searches for an optimization solution and reports whether it is optimal, infeasible or unbounded, or stops at a time or other limit with or without a feasible solution.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="11-solver.html">lesson 11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="spare-capacity" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-spare-capacity">
<h3 id="glossary-name-spare-capacity"><a href="#spare-capacity">Spare capacity (headroom)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The MW a substation or line can still take for a new load or plant without an upgrade.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a19-gis-siting.html">A19</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="spatial-resolution" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-spatial-resolution">
<h3 id="glossary-name-spatial-resolution"><a href="#spatial-resolution">Spatial resolution</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The size of a raster&#x27;s cells: finer cells show smaller features, such as a setback, but need more data and more computing.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a19-gis-siting.html">A19</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="special-ordered-set" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-special-ordered-set">
<h3 id="glossary-name-special-ordered-set"><a href="#special-ordered-set">Special ordered set (SOS2)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A rule in a mixed-integer program that lets at most two neighboring points of a curve be used, so the model can follow a curved line by joining straight pieces.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf5-drawing-the-boundary.html">CF5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="spent-fuel" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-spent-fuel">
<h3 id="glossary-name-spent-fuel"><a href="#spent-fuel">Spent fuel</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Fuel that has been used in a reactor and taken out; it is solid, highly radioactive and still warm, and is kept first in water pools, later in dry casks.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="spillover-effect" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-spillover-effect">
<h3 id="glossary-name-spillover-effect"><a href="#spillover-effect">Spillover</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">When a program also changes the comparison group, for example neighbors copying a habit or projects moving across a border.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m14-did-it-work.html">M14</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="sponsor-equity" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-sponsor-equity">
<h3 id="glossary-name-sponsor-equity"><a href="#sponsor-equity">Sponsor equity</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The developer&#x27;s or owner&#x27;s own money in a project: paid last, so it carries the most risk and keeps what is left.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="x05-project-finance.html">X5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="spp" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-spp">
<h3 id="glossary-name-spp"><a href="#spp">SPP (Southwest Power Pool)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The regional grid operator that runs the transmission grid and wholesale electricity market across much of the central U.S.; the course&#x27;s hourly data come from its area (EIA-930).</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r08-communicating.html">R8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="staged-energization" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-staged-energization">
<h3 id="glossary-name-staged-energization"><a href="#staged-energization">Staged energization</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Switching on part of a large load&#x27;s grid service early and the rest later, as the grid becomes ready.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf7-cost-of-waiting.html">CF7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="staging-area" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-staging-area">
<h3 id="glossary-name-staging-area"><a href="#staging-area">Staging area</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Git&#x27;s list of changes picked for the next commit: git add puts a file&#x27;s current version there.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="stakeholder" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-stakeholder">
<h3 id="glossary-name-stakeholder"><a href="#stakeholder">Stakeholder</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A person or group affected by a study or the decision it informs, or able to affect it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r09-integrity-stakeholders.html">R9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="standard-deviation" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-standard-deviation">
<h3 id="glossary-name-standard-deviation"><a href="#standard-deviation">Standard deviation</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A measure of spread: roughly, how far a typical value lies from the mean.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="b02-python-data.html">B2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="standard-error" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-standard-error">
<h3 id="glossary-name-standard-error"><a href="#standard-error">Standard error</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How far an estimate from a random sample typically lands from the value for the whole set; it shrinks as the sample grows.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k05-probability-statistics.html">K5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="standing-loss" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-standing-loss">
<h3 id="glossary-name-standing-loss"><a href="#standing-loss">Standing loss</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Energy a store loses while it waits, used or not, such as heat leaking from a hot tank; it grows with time, unlike the loss of each charge and discharge.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a08-storage-duration.html">A8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="start-up-cost" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-start-up-cost">
<h3 id="glossary-name-start-up-cost"><a href="#start-up-cost">Start-up cost</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The fuel and wear spent to bring a plant from off to on, paid once per start.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m02-unit-commitment.html">M2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="start-up-time" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-start-up-time">
<h3 id="glossary-name-start-up-time"><a href="#start-up-time">Start-up time</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How long a plant takes to go from shut down to full output; the ramp rate is how fast it changes output once running.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="state-of-charge" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-state-of-charge">
<h3 id="glossary-name-state-of-charge"><a href="#state-of-charge">State of charge</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The energy a battery holds at a given moment, in MWh; it links each hour of a storage schedule to the next.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="09-storage.html">lesson 9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="steam-generator" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-steam-generator">
<h3 id="glossary-name-steam-generator"><a href="#steam-generator">Steam generator</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A heat exchanger in which hot water from a reactor&#x27;s sealed loop boils the water of a second, separate loop into steam.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="steam-turbine" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-steam-turbine">
<h3 id="glossary-name-steam-turbine"><a href="#steam-turbine">Steam turbine</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A turbine spun by high-pressure steam from a boiler or another heat source.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="stock" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-stock">
<h3 id="glossary-name-stock"><a href="#stock">Stock</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An amount that builds up or drains over time, such as water in a reservoir, energy in a battery or CO₂ emitted so far.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f02-systems-and-map.html">F2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="storage-link" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-storage-link">
<h3 id="glossary-name-storage-link"><a href="#storage-link">Storage link (between periods)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">In a model of representative periods, the energy stored at the end of one period carried into the next, so storage can move energy across days or seasons.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r02-literature.html">R2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="stranded-cost" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-stranded-cost">
<h3 id="glossary-name-stranded-cost"><a href="#stranded-cost">Stranded cost</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Money already spent on equipment that is no longer used as planned, such as grid upgrades built for a load that never arrives.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf7-cost-of-waiting.html">CF7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="stress-test" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-stress-test">
<h3 id="glossary-name-stress-test"><a href="#stress-test">Stress test</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Running a system model through a severe event on purpose, to see what breaks and what a defense would change.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a09-hazards.html">A9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="structural-uncertainty" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-structural-uncertainty">
<h3 id="glossary-name-structural-uncertainty"><a href="#structural-uncertainty">Structural uncertainty</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Doubt about how a model is built (its equations, time steps and what it leaves out), which sampling its inputs cannot reveal; compare model forms instead.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r06-uncertainty-properly.html">R6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="stylized-network" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-stylized-network">
<h3 id="glossary-name-stylized-network"><a href="#stylized-network">Stylized network</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A simplified, made-up network built to show how a model behaves, with invented distances and costs rather than a real company&#x27;s map.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf1-supply-chain-microgrids.html">CF1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="substation" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-substation">
<h3 id="glossary-name-substation"><a href="#substation">Substation</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A fenced yard of transformers, breakers and switches where the grid changes voltage and where feeders start.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="substitution-method" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-substitution-method">
<h3 id="glossary-name-substitution-method"><a href="#substitution-method">Substitution method</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A rule for counting primary energy in which each MWh from nuclear, hydro, wind and solar counts as the fuel a thermal power plant would burn to make it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="suitability-score" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-suitability-score">
<h3 id="glossary-name-suitability-score"><a href="#suitability-score">Suitability score</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A cell&#x27;s or a site&#x27;s weighted score in a siting screen, here from 0 to 100: a ranking under stated weights, not a cost and not a verdict.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a19-gis-siting.html">A19</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="sunk-cost" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-sunk-cost">
<h3 id="glossary-name-sunk-cost"><a href="#sunk-cost">Sunk cost</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Money already spent that no choice made now can change, such as what an existing plant cost to build; it drops out when options are compared.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf4-existing-reactors-hydrogen.html">CF4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="supply-diversity" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-supply-diversity">
<h3 id="glossary-name-supply-diversity"><a href="#supply-diversity">Supply diversity</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How evenly the energy supply is spread over different sources, so that losing one does not lose most of it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a22-tradeoff-explorer.html">A22</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="supply-stack" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-supply-stack">
<h3 id="glossary-name-supply-stack"><a href="#supply-stack">Supply stack</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">All the offers to sell power in one hour, lined up from the cheapest to the most expensive.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="08-merit-order.html">lesson 8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="supply-chain-tier" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-supply-chain-tier">
<h3 id="glossary-name-supply-chain-tier"><a href="#supply-chain-tier">Supply-chain tier</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">One level of a supply chain, such as factories, then warehouses, then stores: a three-tier chain has all three, a two-tier chain two of them.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf1-supply-chain-microgrids.html">CF1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="surrogate-model" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-surrogate-model">
<h3 id="glossary-name-surrogate-model"><a href="#surrogate-model">Surrogate model</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A cheap stand-in for a model or measurement that is costly to run, fitted to a few samples and then used in its place.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m09-surrogates-uq.html">M9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="synchronous-grid" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-synchronous-grid">
<h3 id="glossary-name-synchronous-grid"><a href="#synchronous-grid">Synchronous grid</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A connected AC network whose generators and other equipment run at one shared electrical frequency; the Lower 48 states have three main ones, called interconnections.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f01-five-scales.html">F1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="synthetic-data" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-synthetic-data">
<h3 id="glossary-name-synthetic-data"><a href="#synthetic-data">Synthetic data</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Invented values made to look realistic, used in place of real records so that a model can be shown and shared.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf1-supply-chain-microgrids.html">CF1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="synthetic-sample" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-synthetic-sample">
<h3 id="glossary-name-synthetic-sample"><a href="#synthetic-sample">Synthetic sample</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A few invented records with the same columns and realistic values as data that cannot be shared, so others can run the code without the real data.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r09-integrity-stakeholders.html">R9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="system-boundary" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-system-boundary">
<h3 id="glossary-name-system-boundary"><a href="#system-boundary">System boundary</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The line that decides which parts, costs and emissions a study counts and which it leaves out.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="n01-news-lens.html">N1</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-t" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-t">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-t">T</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="target-seeking-scenario" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-target-seeking-scenario">
<h3 id="glossary-name-target-seeking-scenario"><a href="#target-seeking-scenario">Target-seeking scenario</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A scenario that starts from a goal, such as a carbon budget, and works out what it would take to meet it; the IEA calls this kind normative.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a20-national-scenarios.html">A20</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="tariff" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-tariff">
<h3 id="glossary-name-tariff"><a href="#tariff">Tariff</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The rule for calculating electricity bills: fixed charges, prices per kWh, or both.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a22-tradeoff-explorer.html">A22</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="tax-base" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-tax-base">
<h3 id="glossary-name-tax-base"><a href="#tax-base">Tax base</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The total value a local government can tax, such as the assessed value of homes, businesses and power plants in a county.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a13-fairness-jobs.html">A13</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="tax-equity" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-tax-equity">
<h3 id="glossary-name-tax-equity"><a href="#tax-equity">Tax equity</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Money from an investor with a large tax bill, put into a project in exchange for most of its tax credits and depreciation, plus some cash.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="x05-project-finance.html">X5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="techno-economic-analysis" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-techno-economic-analysis">
<h3 id="glossary-name-techno-economic-analysis"><a href="#techno-economic-analysis">Techno-economic analysis (TEA)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Estimating what a technology costs and earns from its engineering design, its prices and its operating pattern.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r10-question-studio.html">R10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="techno-economic-optimization" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-techno-economic-optimization">
<h3 id="glossary-name-techno-economic-optimization"><a href="#techno-economic-optimization">Techno-economic optimization</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A model that compares equipment sizes and ways of running them by both their performance and their cost, and picks the best for a stated goal.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f07-microgrids.html">F7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="technology-readiness" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-technology-readiness">
<h3 id="glossary-name-technology-readiness"><a href="#technology-readiness">Technology readiness level (TRL)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A scale from 1 (basic principles described) to 9 (proven in operation) for how mature a technology or method is.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="x02-fossil-transition.html">X2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="telemetry" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-telemetry">
<h3 id="glossary-name-telemetry"><a href="#telemetry">Telemetry</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Measurements sent automatically from plants and substations to the grid operator.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="b02-python-data.html">B2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="temperature-lift" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-temperature-lift">
<h3 id="glossary-name-temperature-lift"><a href="#temperature-lift">Temperature lift</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How far a heat pump raises heat: its delivery temperature minus its source temperature, in kelvin (a difference of 1 K equals 1 °C).</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a15-efficiency-electrification.html">A15</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="terawatt-hour" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-terawatt-hour">
<h3 id="glossary-name-terawatt-hour"><a href="#terawatt-hour">Terawatt-hour (TWh)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A unit of energy equal to a billion kilowatt-hours, used for the yearly electricity use of regions and countries.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="01-power-energy.html">lesson 1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="thermal-rating" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-thermal-rating">
<h3 id="glossary-name-thermal-rating"><a href="#thermal-rating">Thermal rating</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The most current, or MVA at the line&#x27;s voltage, that a line or transformer can carry before its wires get too hot and sag.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a17-physical-feasibility.html">A17</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="thermal-storage" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-thermal-storage">
<h3 id="glossary-name-thermal-storage"><a href="#thermal-storage">Thermal storage</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Storing energy as heat, for example in tanks of hot molten salt, to use it hours later.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.html">CF2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="tie-rule" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-tie-rule">
<h3 id="glossary-name-tie-rule"><a href="#tie-rule">Tie rule</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A stated way to pick one answer when several plans cost exactly the same, usually tiny costs that are left out of the reported results.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="sb3-city-planner.html">SB3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="time-slice" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-time-slice">
<h3 id="glossary-name-time-slice"><a href="#time-slice">Time slice</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A group of hours, such as winter nights, that a planning model treats as one, weighted by how many hours it stands for.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="sb4-pathway-explorer.html">SB4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="time-step" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-time-step">
<h3 id="glossary-name-time-step"><a href="#time-step">Time step</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The length of one step in a model or dataset, such as five minutes, an hour or a year.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r03-system-and-method.html">R3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="time-of-use-tariff" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-time-of-use-tariff">
<span id="time-of-use" class="lx-glossary-alias"></span>
<h3 id="glossary-name-time-of-use-tariff"><a href="#time-of-use-tariff">Time-of-use tariff</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A retail electricity price that changes with the hour of the day, higher at peak times and lower off-peak.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a04-retail-tariffs.html">A4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="time-series-aggregation" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-time-series-aggregation">
<h3 id="glossary-name-time-series-aggregation"><a href="#time-series-aggregation">Time-series aggregation</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Shrinking a long series, such as a year of hours, to a few representative periods that a model can solve quickly.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r02-literature.html">R2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="tolling-agreement" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-tolling-agreement">
<h3 id="glossary-name-tolling-agreement"><a href="#tolling-agreement">Tolling agreement</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A contract in which the buyer pays the owner of a plant a fixed fee for the right to run it, and keeps what it earns.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a02-contracts-risk.html">A2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="coal-equivalent" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-coal-equivalent">
<h3 id="glossary-name-coal-equivalent"><a href="#coal-equivalent">Ton of coal equivalent (tce)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An energy unit equal to the heat in one metric ton of standard coal, fixed by convention at 29.3076 GJ; China&#x27;s energy statistics count in it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="oil-equivalent" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-oil-equivalent">
<h3 id="glossary-name-oil-equivalent"><a href="#oil-equivalent">Ton of oil equivalent (toe)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An energy unit equal to the heat in one metric ton of crude oil, fixed by convention at 41.868 GJ; ktoe is a thousand of them, Mtoe (Brazil&#x27;s Mtep) a million.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="tornado-chart" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-tornado-chart">
<h3 id="glossary-name-tornado-chart"><a href="#tornado-chart">Tornado chart</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A chart that ranks inputs by how far a result moves when each input is swung from a low to a high value, one at a time.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="07-cost.html">lesson 7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="tracked-file" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-tracked-file">
<h3 id="glossary-name-tracked-file"><a href="#tracked-file">Tracked file</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A file Git already knows, because it is in the last commit or the staging area; a new file stays untracked until git add.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="trading-hub" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-trading-hub">
<h3 id="glossary-name-trading-hub"><a href="#trading-hub">Trading hub</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A pricing point where many contracts are settled, priced as an average over many nodes of the grid.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a02-contracts-risk.html">A2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="transactive-energy" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-transactive-energy">
<h3 id="glossary-name-transactive-energy"><a href="#transactive-energy">Transactive energy</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Buying and selling electricity among many small participants, such as homes and firms with their own generation, as well as with the grid.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a07-flexible-demand.html">A7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="transfer-payment" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-transfer-payment">
<span id="transfer" class="lx-glossary-alias"></span>
<h3 id="glossary-name-transfer-payment"><a href="#transfer-payment">Transfer</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A payment that moves money from one group to another, such as a carbon payment to the government or a credit to a plant owner, without using anything up.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a12-policy-instruments.html">A12</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="transformer" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-transformer">
<h3 id="glossary-name-transformer"><a href="#transformer">Transformer</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A device with two coils that raises or lowers an alternating voltage, such as from 18 kV to 345 kV at a plant or from 12.47 kV to 240/120 V near a home.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="transmission" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-transmission">
<h3 id="glossary-name-transmission"><a href="#transmission">Transmission</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The high-voltage part of the grid (115 to 765 kV in the U.S.) that carries power over long distances between plants, regions and substations.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="transport-model" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-transport-model">
<h3 id="glossary-name-transport-model"><a href="#transport-model">Transport model</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A network model in which each link can carry any flow up to its limit, with no power-flow physics: power goes where the cheapest routes allow.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="sb2-grid-room.html">SB2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="triangulation" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-triangulation">
<h3 id="glossary-name-triangulation"><a href="#triangulation">Triangulation</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Checking a finding against a second source or a second method, so that it does not rest on one kind of evidence alone.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cr-your-own-study.html">CR</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="truncated-axis" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-truncated-axis">
<h3 id="glossary-name-truncated-axis"><a href="#truncated-axis">Truncated axis</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A chart axis that starts above zero; on a bar chart it makes differences look larger than they are.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r08-communicating.html">R8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="turbine" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-turbine">
<h3 id="glossary-name-turbine"><a href="#turbine">Turbine</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A machine whose blades are pushed round by moving gas, steam, water or wind, turning a shaft.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="turbine-crossover" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-turbine-crossover">
<h3 id="glossary-name-turbine-crossover"><a href="#turbine-crossover">Turbine crossover</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The pipe that carries steam from a high-pressure turbine to a low-pressure turbine; steam taken there has already done part of its work.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf5-drawing-the-boundary.html">CF5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="two-stage-stochastic-program" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-two-stage-stochastic-program">
<h3 id="glossary-name-two-stage-stochastic-program"><a href="#two-stage-stochastic-program">Two-stage stochastic program</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An optimization model that chooses the here-and-now decisions and each branch&#x27;s recourse together, to minimize the expected cost over all branches.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m08-stochastic-robust.html">M8</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-u" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-u">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-u">U</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="unbounded" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-unbounded">
<h3 id="glossary-name-unbounded"><a href="#unbounded">Unbounded</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Said of a model whose goal can improve without limit, which usually means a rule is missing.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="10-write-it-down.html">lesson 10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="unbundling" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-unbundling">
<h3 id="glossary-name-unbundling"><a href="#unbundling">Unbundling</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Separating the grid from the making and selling of electricity, so that different companies, or legally separate parts of one, run each.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f10-nations-differ.html">F10</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="ufls" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-ufls">
<h3 id="glossary-name-ufls"><a href="#ufls">Under-frequency load shedding</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Relays that automatically disconnect blocks of customers when the frequency falls to a set level, to save the rest of the grid.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="03-balancing.html">lesson 3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="unit-commitment" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-unit-commitment">
<h3 id="glossary-name-unit-commitment"><a href="#unit-commitment">Unit commitment</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Deciding which plants are on in each hour, before deciding how much each one produces.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="11-solver.html">lesson 11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="unserved-energy" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-unserved-energy">
<h3 id="glossary-name-unserved-energy"><a href="#unserved-energy">Unserved energy</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Demand that could not be met, so some customers lost power.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="00-grid-operator.html">lesson 0</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="uplift" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-uplift">
<h3 id="glossary-name-uplift"><a href="#uplift">Uplift payment</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A payment outside the market price that covers costs a scheduled plant cannot recover at the price, such as start-up and no-load costs; also called a make-whole payment.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m02-unit-commitment.html">M2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="uprate" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-uprate">
<h3 id="glossary-name-uprate"><a href="#uprate">Uprate (of a line or link)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Raising the most power a line or link may carry, for example with new conductors or a second circuit.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="sb2-grid-room.html">SB2</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="uranium-235" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-uranium-235">
<h3 id="glossary-name-uranium-235"><a href="#uranium-235">Uranium-235</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The form of uranium whose atoms split easily when they catch a slow neutron; natural uranium holds only a small share of it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f05-nuclear-basics.html">F5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="useful-energy" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-useful-energy">
<h3 id="glossary-name-useful-energy"><a href="#useful-energy">Useful energy</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Energy a device delivers in the wanted form, such as heat, light or motion; a heat pump&#x27;s delivered heat includes heat drawn from the outdoor air, not only the energy bought.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f03-energy-services.html">F3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="utility-scale" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-utility-scale">
<h3 id="glossary-name-utility-scale"><a href="#utility-scale">Utility-scale</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Large enough to sell power to the grid; in EIA&#x27;s statistics, plants of at least 1 MW.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r08-communicating.html">R8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="utm" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-utm">
<h3 id="glossary-name-utm"><a href="#utm">UTM (Universal Transverse Mercator)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A set of 60 north-to-south zones, each a flat map in meters that keeps distances close to true inside the zone.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r04-data.html">R4</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-v" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-v">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-v">V</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="validation" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-validation">
<h3 id="glossary-name-validation"><a href="#validation">Validation</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Checking that a model represents the real system well enough for the question it is used to answer.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="b03-read-check-formulation.html">B3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="value-of-coupling" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-value-of-coupling">
<h3 id="glossary-name-value-of-coupling"><a href="#value-of-coupling">Value of coupling</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How much cheaper a system is with devices that link its carriers than with each carrier supplied on its own, judged as a difference of optimal costs.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m04-storage-multienergy.html">M4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="value-of-information" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-value-of-information">
<h3 id="glossary-name-value-of-information"><a href="#value-of-information">Value of information</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How much a decision-maker would gain, on average, by learning an uncertain quantity before deciding; its upper limit is the value of a perfect forecast.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r06-uncertainty-properly.html">R6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="value-of-lost-load" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-value-of-lost-load">
<h3 id="glossary-name-value-of-lost-load"><a href="#value-of-lost-load">Value of lost load</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">What a customer loses when power is cut, per hour or per kWh not delivered; it differs by customer and by how long the outage lasts.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a14-microgrid-value.html">A14</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="value-of-stochastic-solution" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-value-of-stochastic-solution">
<h3 id="glossary-name-value-of-stochastic-solution"><a href="#value-of-stochastic-solution">Value of the stochastic solution (VSS)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How much the stochastic program&#x27;s plan saves, in expectation, against the plan built for the average future.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m08-stochastic-robust.html">M8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="variable-om" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-variable-om">
<h3 id="glossary-name-variable-om"><a href="#variable-om">Variable O&amp;M</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Operation and maintenance costs, apart from fuel, that grow with every megawatt-hour a plant makes.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="07-cost.html">lesson 7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="variable-renewables" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-variable-renewables">
<h3 id="glossary-name-variable-renewables"><a href="#variable-renewables">Variable renewables</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Wind and solar power, whose output follows the weather: they can be turned down but not up.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="00-grid-operator.html">lesson 0</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="variogram" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-variogram">
<h3 id="glossary-name-variogram"><a href="#variogram">Variogram</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A measure of how much values at two places differ, on average, as a function of the distance between them; here, across a wind plant&#x27;s turbines.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf8-power-curves-from-scarce-data.html">CF8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="vector" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-vector">
<h3 id="glossary-name-vector"><a href="#vector">Vector</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An ordered list of numbers, such as a plan&#x27;s outputs, in which the position of each number carries its meaning.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k06-vectors-matrices.html">K6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="verification" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-verification">
<h3 id="glossary-name-verification"><a href="#verification">Verification</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Checking that a model&#x27;s equations and code implement the intended model correctly, with tests such as units, the energy balance and hand-solved cases.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="b03-read-check-formulation.html">B3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="version-control" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-version-control">
<h3 id="glossary-name-version-control"><a href="#version-control">Version control</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Keeping selected recorded versions of a project&#x27;s files, with who changed what and why, so any recorded version can be compared or brought back.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="version-pin" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-version-pin">
<h3 id="glossary-name-version-pin"><a href="#version-pin">Version pin</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A line such as pandas==2.2.3 in requirements.txt that asks the installer for one exact version of a package.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="vertically-integrated-utility" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-vertically-integrated-utility">
<h3 id="glossary-name-vertically-integrated-utility"><a href="#vertically-integrated-utility">Vertically integrated utility</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An electric utility that owns and runs the power plants, transmission and distribution in its service territory, as Kansas&#x27;s investor-owned utilities do; its rates are approved by the state regulator.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f09-city-energy.html">F9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="vintage" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-vintage">
<h3 id="glossary-name-vintage"><a href="#vintage">Vintage</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The year a plant was built: in a multi-decade model each vintage keeps its own cost and runs until its life ends.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="sb4-pathway-explorer.html">SB4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="virtual-power-plant" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-virtual-power-plant">
<h3 id="glossary-name-virtual-power-plant"><a href="#virtual-power-plant">Virtual power plant</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Many small devices, such as batteries, thermostats and chargers, controlled together and offered to the grid as one resource.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a07-flexible-demand.html">A7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="voltage" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-voltage">
<h3 id="glossary-name-voltage"><a href="#voltage">Voltage</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The electrical push that drives current through a wire, measured in volts (V); 1 kilovolt (kV) is 1,000 V.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f06-grid-and-outages.html">F6</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="voltage-angle" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-voltage-angle">
<h3 id="glossary-name-voltage-angle"><a href="#voltage-angle">Voltage angle</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">How far the alternating voltage at one bus runs ahead of the voltage at the reference bus, whose angle is set to zero; in DC power flow a line&#x27;s flow is proportional to the angle difference across it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m01-dispatch-to-lmp.html">M1</a></p>
</article>
</section>
<section class="lx-glossary-group" id="glossary-w" aria-labelledby="glossary-heading-w">
<h2 id="glossary-heading-w">W</h2>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="wait-and-see" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-wait-and-see">
<h3 id="glossary-name-wait-and-see"><a href="#wait-and-see">Wait-and-see problem</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The planning problem solved as if the future were known: one best plan for each branch, which no real planner can choose in advance.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="m08-stochastic-robust.html">M8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="waste-heat" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-waste-heat">
<h3 id="glossary-name-waste-heat"><a href="#waste-heat">Waste heat</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Heat a power plant cannot turn into electricity and releases to the air or to cooling water.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="f04-power-plants.html">F4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="water-consumption" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-water-consumption">
<h3 id="glossary-name-water-consumption"><a href="#water-consumption">Water consumption</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Water taken and not returned, mostly lost to evaporation, so it is no longer available downstream.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a11-lca-nexus.html">A11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="water-withdrawal" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-water-withdrawal">
<h3 id="glossary-name-water-withdrawal"><a href="#water-withdrawal">Water withdrawal</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Water taken from a river, lake or aquifer, of which the part not returned is consumption; how much returns depends on the cooling system.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a11-lca-nexus.html">A11</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="watt-hour" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-watt-hour">
<h3 id="glossary-name-watt-hour"><a href="#watt-hour">Watt-hour (Wh)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A unit of energy: one watt kept up for one hour; 1,000 Wh make one kilowatt-hour.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="01-power-energy.html">lesson 1</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="weather-zone" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-weather-zone">
<h3 id="glossary-name-weather-zone"><a href="#weather-zone">Weather zone</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">One of the areas into which a grid operator divides its region for weather and demand forecasts; ERCOT has eight.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf3-hydrogen-under-uncertainty.html">CF3</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="weatherization" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-weatherization">
<h3 id="glossary-name-weatherization"><a href="#weatherization">Weatherization</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Air sealing, insulation and similar work on a building&#x27;s shell that cuts the heat it loses, so it needs less heating.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a18-city-plan.html">A18</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="web-mercator" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-web-mercator">
<h3 id="glossary-name-web-mercator"><a href="#web-mercator">Web Mercator</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The projection most web maps use: good for viewing, but it stretches distances and areas more the farther a place is from the equator.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="r04-data.html">R4</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="weibull" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-weibull">
<h3 id="glossary-name-weibull"><a href="#weibull">Weibull distribution</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A curve often used for the share of a year&#x27;s hours at each wind speed; its shape k (no unit) sets how spread out the speeds are, and its scale c, in m/s, sets how high they run.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf8-power-curves-from-scarce-data.html">CF8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="wacc" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-wacc">
<h3 id="glossary-name-wacc"><a href="#wacc">Weighted average cost of capital (WACC)</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The blended return a project must pay its lenders and its owners, used as the project&#x27;s discount rate.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="07-cost.html">lesson 7</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="weighted-overlay" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-weighted-overlay">
<h3 id="glossary-name-weighted-overlay"><a href="#weighted-overlay">Weighted overlay</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">Combining several criterion maps cell by cell: each criterion is scored from 0 to 1, multiplied by its weight, and the results are added into one suitability map.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a19-gis-siting.html">A19</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="weighted-sum" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-weighted-sum">
<h3 id="glossary-name-weighted-sum"><a href="#weighted-sum">Weighted sum</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A way to combine several goals into one score by adding them up, each multiplied by a weight.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="12-trade-offs.html">lesson 12</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="well-to-gate" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-well-to-gate">
<h3 id="glossary-name-well-to-gate"><a href="#well-to-gate">Well-to-gate</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">An emissions boundary from producing the inputs, such as gas or electricity, to hydrogen leaving the plant; delivery and use are outside it.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a16-hydrogen-ptx.html">A16</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="wet-bulb-temperature" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-wet-bulb-temperature">
<h3 id="glossary-name-wet-bulb-temperature"><a href="#wet-bulb-temperature">Wet-bulb temperature</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The lowest temperature evaporating water can reach in the air at hand, which combines heat and humidity; when it is high, chillers and cooling towers reject heat less well and deliver less, which is called derating.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf5-drawing-the-boundary.html">CF5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="wholesale-price" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-wholesale-price">
<h3 id="glossary-name-wholesale-price"><a href="#wholesale-price">Wholesale price</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">The price at which electricity is traded between power plants and the companies that sell it to customers, often set hour by hour.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="08-merit-order.html">lesson 8</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="public-safety-power-shutoff" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-public-safety-power-shutoff">
<h3 id="glossary-name-public-safety-power-shutoff"><a href="#public-safety-power-shutoff">Wildfire safety shutoff</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A utility switching off power lines in dry, windy weather so that they cannot start a fire; the customers on those lines lose power.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="a09-hazards.html">A9</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="willans-line" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-willans-line">
<h3 id="glossary-name-willans-line"><a href="#willans-line">Willans line</a></h3>
<p class="lx-glossary-definition">A straight-line rule for a turbine&#x27;s steam use against its output; here it gives the electricity lost for each unit of steam taken out of the turbine.</p>
<p class="lx-glossary-lesson">Learn in <a href="cf5-drawing-the-boundary.html">CF5</a></p>
</article>
<article class="lx-glossary-entry" id="winterization" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="glossary-name-winterization">
<h3 id="glossary-name-winterization"><a href="#winterization">Winterization</a></h3>
